title: Media storage: a picture kept after one retryable removal failure stays kept until --retry-failed, holding import drains
body:
## What happens

A picture whose removal check fails once with a retryable service error is marked `kept:<signature>` in `_seoprostack_storage_local` (`local_result()`, "One attachment must not hold up the whole library"). Nothing clears that mark except `wp seoprostack media-storage upload --retry-failed` (or switching "Remove local copies after upload" off and on), which drops every kept mark on the site. Until a person runs it, the picture keeps all its local files.

SEO Pro Directory's import drain waits for each picture's local files to go, in order, so one kept picture holds its part in `draining` until the job's one-hour no-progress stop, and resuming only restarts the hour. `remove_local_now()` / `remove_local_many()` answer `storage_kept` for it, so callers that ask SEO Pro Stack to remove it cannot either.

Observed on 6 November 2026 (SEO Pro Stack 1.3.160, SEO Pro Directory 0.4.118): the last part of a 27-part regional import stood 41 minutes on one attachment, the only kept picture on that site. It was `uploaded`, and every one of its 11 local files (JPEG sizes plus WebP/AVIF copies) was in its `_seoprostack_storage` record. The site's last storage error at the time was "The kept original is in use by another request. Try again shortly." Dropping that one picture's kept mark let the next removal pass take it; the part drained and the job ended within 4 minutes. Another importing site had one kept picture as well.

## Expected

A kept mark from a retryable failure is revisited on its own after a while, as the comment beside it intends ("retry-failed or a changed connection can revisit the mark"). An import should not need a person to notice it.

## Suggested fix

In `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`:

1. When `local_result()` marks a picture kept after a retryable failure, record when (for example `kept:<signature>:<time>`, or a separate meta key) instead of a permanent mark.
2. In the removal pass and in `remove_local_now()` / `remove_local_many()`, treat a retryable kept mark older than a short interval (for example 10 minutes) as not kept: check the picture again, keeping the existing mismatch/change handling in `removal_stopped()` permanent.
3. Leave the marks `restore_attachment()` and `removal_stopped()` set (mismatch or change) as they are: those need a person or a new upload.

Pattern to follow: the `LOCAL_WAIT` pause after a busy original, which already expires on its own.

## Verification

- Make one picture's removal fail once with a retryable error (or set its mark by hand with an old time), with "Remove local copies after upload" on: within the interval plus one batch its local files are removed and its mark becomes the signature, with no `--retry-failed`.
- A mismatch (`removal_stopped()`) still keeps its files.
- `wp seoprostack media-storage status` shows no kept pictures after a full import; an import whose pictures all upload runs to the end with no one-hour drain stop.

Related: #1256 (a removed picture whose later WebP/AVIF copies stay on disk also holds a drain).

title: Old slugs: redundant() for one post without the cross-table OR (170 ms a slug change on 7,436 old slugs)
body:
## What

`SEOProStack_Old_Slugs::redundant($post_id)` runs on every slug change (`post_updated`). Its last query, "another published post of the same type now has the slug", filters with `(%d = 0 OR pm.post_id = %d OR o.ID = %d)`. For one post the OR spans two tables, so MySQL can use neither the `post_id` index nor `o.ID`: it reads every `_wp_old_slug` row and joins each to `wp_posts` twice. The cost grows with the site's old slugs, and an importer that publishes thousands of posts pays it once per post.

## Evidence (6 November 2026, live import on a PSD stack, SEO Pro Directory 0.4.120)

`import-profile-queries.php` (PSD repository, `scripts/`), 120 s beside the import: 10 calls, 1.7 s, **170 ms each**, via `SEOProStack_Old_Slugs::redundant < post_updated < wp_insert_post < wp_update_post < SEOProDirectory_Outscraper_Import::process_row`. That stack had 7,436 `_wp_old_slug` rows (a larger one 21,192). Most were SEO Pro Directory's leftover temporary slugs, which wpallstars/seoprodirectory#435 removes, so on those stacks the scan becomes small; a site with many real old slugs still pays it on every slug change.

## How

For `$id > 0`, replace the one OR query with two indexed ones and merge the rows as now:

1. This post's old slugs that another published post of the same type now has: `WHERE pm.meta_key = %s AND pm.post_id = %d` (uses `post_id`), joined to `o` on type and `post_name`.
2. Other posts' old slugs equal to this post's current slug: `WHERE pm.meta_key = %s AND pm.meta_value = %s` with the post's own `post_name` (reads only `_wp_old_slug` rows, no join before the filter), joined to `p` for a dateless type and `p.ID <> %d`.

Keep the `$id = 0` (sweep) query as it is.

## Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-old-slugs.php` (`redundant()`)

## Acceptance

- For a post ID, the rows returned (meta ID and post ID pairs) are the same as the current query's on a test site with old slugs of several posts and types, including a slug taken by another published post and one of this post's own old slugs taken by another post.
- `EXPLAIN` of each new query uses an index on `wp_postmeta` (`post_id` or `meta_key`) and no full join of all old-slug rows.
- PHP lint, PHPCS and PHPStan as in CI.

title: Speed: load Simple Cloudflare Turnstile when a form comes near; its WooCommerce script only on checkout
body:
## What

Speed, on by default: load Simple Cloudflare Turnstile's `api.js` when one of its widgets comes near the screen or a field of its form gets focus, and load its WooCommerce script (`cfturnstile-woo-js`) only on WooCommerce checkout pages.

## Why

Simple Cloudflare Turnstile (recommended in `admin/data/free-plugins.php`) prints its scripts on every page with a widget, including a login form in a closed Kadence header account drawer. On a Kadence home page with WooCommerce (Simple Cloudflare Turnstile 1.44.5, PageSpeed Insights mobile, 6 November 2026):

- `challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js` (28 KB), then Cloudflare's challenge, for a widget nobody has opened.
- `cfturnstile-woo-js` (`js/integrations/woocommerce.js`) depends on `wp-data`, so WordPress also prints `react`, `react-dom`, `react-jsx-runtime`, `wp-element`, `wp-data`, `wp-compose`, `wp-hooks`, `wp-i18n` and 9 more: 17 extra requests, about 100 KB. That script only keeps the classic and block checkout widgets valid and handles the checkout's "show login" toggle.

Same idea as `SEOProStack_Fluentforms_Turnstile` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-fluentforms-turnstile.php`, #1210), which does this for Fluent Forms' own Turnstile.

## How

1. New feature class (setting `turnstile_later`, Speed tab, on by default), active when Simple Cloudflare Turnstile is, front end only (not the admin, `wp-login.php`, feeds, AJAX, REST).
2. `api.js` later: Simple Cloudflare Turnstile 1.44+ registers `cfturnstile` as `…/turnstile/v0/api.js?render=explicit&onload=cfturnstileOnload` with its render queue (`cfturnstile_api_bootstrap()`) and token refresh as inline `before` scripts. In `script_loader_tag` for that handle, when the address is exactly that and `cfturnstile_api_bootstrap` exists, keep the inline scripts and replace only the external `<script src>` with a loader: add the same `api.js` once a `.cf-turnstile` comes within 600 px of the screen, a field of a form holding one gets focus, or the page has no IntersectionObserver. The queue renders queued widgets from `cfturnstileOnload`, so widgets render as before. Older versions, other addresses or another plugin's `cfturnstile` handle: left alone.
3. WooCommerce script only on checkout: at `wp_print_footer_scripts` priority 9 (just before WordPress prints footer scripts), dequeue `cfturnstile-woo-js` unless `is_checkout()` (pay-for-order included) or the post has the checkout block or shortcode. Its `wp-data` dependency then goes too, unless something else needs it.
4. README feature section, Speed settings text, changelog. Recommended speed settings when the plugin is active, as for the Fluent Forms one.

## Files

- New `includes/features/class-seoprostack-turnstile-later.php` (model: `class-seoprostack-fluentforms-turnstile.php`).
- Feature registration where the other Speed features are registered (see how `SEOProStack_Fluentforms_Turnstile` is loaded).
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

- Test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`) with Kadence, WooCommerce, Simple Cloudflare Turnstile 1.44.5 (test keys), Turnstile on the WordPress login form and a header account drawer showing it: home page loads no `api.js` and none of the React or `wp-data` files; opening the drawer and focusing a field loads `api.js`, the widget renders and a login succeeds.
- WooCommerce checkout (classic and block) with Turnstile on: `cfturnstile-woo-js` prints, the widget renders, an order goes through and a failed one gets a fresh token.
- `wp-login.php` unchanged. Feature off: tags as before. `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Live Kadence home page with WooCommerce: PageSpeed request count and transfer size before and after.

title: Speed: load Google Maps embeds when they come near, not with the page
body:
## The problem

FlyingPress's lazy loading holds iframes back until the visitor scrolls near them: it moves `src` to `data-lazy-src`. After a Kadence site moves from FlyingPress to SEO Pro Stack, embeds rely on the browser's own `loading="lazy"` instead. Chrome starts loading lazy iframes well before they reach the screen, so on desktop a Google Maps embed in a lower section of a home page now loads with the page. In this case it was the Kadence Blocks Google Maps block, using the Embed API.

PageSpeed desktop, home page, map in a lower section:

- Google Maps: 16 requests, about 490 KB transferred, about 360 ms of main-thread time, and 2 long tasks totalling about 195 ms.
- The map also loads its own Google Fonts stylesheets.

On mobile the same map stays out of the first load (0 Maps requests in Lighthouse mobile), so this is mainly a desktop cost.

## What SEO Pro Stack could do

The same approach as **Load Fluent Forms' Turnstile when a form comes near** (#1210): print Google Maps embeds without `src` (kept in `data-src`), and set it when the map comes within about 600 px of the screen or on the first interaction. Keep `width`, `height` and the block's container so nothing shifts, plus a `<noscript>` copy. Leave a map in the first screen alone. Other heavy embeds could follow the same rule later.

## Plugin it would replace

FlyingPress (its lazy loading for iframes).

## Anything else

Seen with Kadence Blocks 3.8.1.1, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.3 and SEO Pro Stack 1.3.161. In a local desktop Chrome with site isolation, the map's scripts run in their own process, so the main-thread cost shows mostly in PageSpeed; the roughly 480 KB downloaded during page load shows in every run.

title: Deploy check: pin the home fetch to the origin (LiteSpeed host behind Cloudflare answers the host's own fetch with 403)
body:
## What

`scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` `home_check()` (about line 591) fetches `<home>/?deploy-check=<stamp>-<n>` from the host itself, through normal DNS. On a LiteSpeed host with Cloudflare in front, the origin answers that request with its own 403 page. The same address fetched from anywhere else answers 200.

Seen in the 2026-11-06 rollouts (SEO Pro Stack 1.3.162 and 1.3.163, SEO Pro Cookie Consent 1.0.15) across about 70 install lines on one Hostinger host. Most Cloudflare-proxied sites reported `home=403 cache=cf-cache-status:dynamic`, and the same site varied between runs. The check treats 4xx as a possible firewall (a warning, not a failure), so on those sites the home fetch verified nothing. Installs without Cloudflare reported `home=200`. The full WordPress load, the cron runs and the web PHP log were still checked.

Evidence, one site:

- From the host, `curl -sD- 'https://<site>/?deploy-check=x'` returns `HTTP/2 403`, `server: cloudflare`, `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC`, with LiteSpeed's "403 Forbidden" page as the body. `DYNAMIC` means the request reached the origin, so the 403 is the origin's, not a Cloudflare firewall rule.
- From the host, the plain address with no query string returns 200 `cf-cache-status: HIT`, answered by Cloudflare's cache without reaching the origin.
- From outside the host, the same `?deploy-check=` address returns 200 `x-litespeed-cache: miss`.

So the host refuses uncached requests that loop back to it through the CDN. Visitors are not affected. Keep pages cached is not affected either, because it pins its requests to the origin.

## Fix

Pin the home fetch to the origin, as Keep pages cached does: `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php` `resolver()` (lines 263-302) uses LiteSpeed Cache's Server IP, or else the address learned from a web request (#1243), through `CURLOPT_RESOLVE`. In the shell check:

- Read the address on the host from LiteSpeed Cache's Server IP option (`wp option get litespeed.conf.server_ip`), or else SEO Pro Stack's learned address.
- Fetch with `curl --resolve "<host>:<port>:<ip>"`.
- Fall back to plain DNS when neither address exists, and keep the 403-as-warning rule for that fallback only.

title: Deploy check: a cron could_not_set race it caused itself counts as a new log error
body:
## What

During the 1.3.162 rollout, one busy network install (4 sites) was reported as `FAIL` with `new_log_lines=2`. Both lines came from `wp-cron.php` in the same second that the deploy check ran the plugin's events with `wp cron event run` (`run_site_cron()` in `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`, about line 551):

```
Cron reschedule event error for hook: seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_check, Error code: could_not_set, Error message: The cron event list could not be saved., Data: {"schedule":"seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_check","args":[],"interval":300}
Cron unschedule event error for hook: seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_check, Error code: could_not_set, ...
```

WordPress logs these when `_set_cron_array()` has nothing to save because another process has just rescheduled the same event. Here the deploy's forced run and the site's own cron runner handled the same five-minute event at once. The plugin only schedules that event when it is missing (`SEOProStack_Keep_Pages_Cached::sync_check()`), so the deploy check caused the race; it is not a plugin fault. All four sites loaded, every cron event ran, and every home page answered 200. The install stayed on the new version.

## Fix

When counting new web-log lines, treat `Cron (reschedule|unschedule) event error for hook: <hook>, Error code: could_not_set` as a warning when `<hook>` is one of the hooks `run_site_cron()` has just run (it already has the list). Show it as, for example, `WARN cron race <hook>`. Count every other new line as before.

## Files

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: `run_site_cron()` and the code that counts `new_log_lines`. This is a core file, so take the change to the starter as well (`STANDARDS.md` → Agent docs; the current drift is #1290).
- `RELEASING.md`, the paragraph on `cron=N/M` (about lines 176-185): mention the race warning.

## Verification

- ShellCheck on `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: no findings.
- Feed the log-counting function a log holding one race line for a hook it ran, one race line for a hook it did not run, and one PHP warning. The first is a warning; the other two fail.

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`

title: Hosting needs: warn when Cloudflare keeps copies of pages that LiteSpeed Cache purges; preset turns on Clear Cloudflare cache
body:
## What

Where Cloudflare caches a site's pages (a Cache Rule that caches HTML, as on many LiteSpeed sites behind Cloudflare), purging LiteSpeed Cache does not clear Cloudflare's copies. After a plugin update, a deploy or a purge, visitors keep getting the old pages until Cloudflare's edge TTL ends (2 hours by default), with the old markup and the old `?ver=` addresses.

Evidence, 6 November 2026, 20 Kadence sites on one LiteSpeed host, all behind Cloudflare:

- Home pages answered `cf-cache-status: HIT` (or MISS then HIT) with `age` up to 6,930 s, carrying the origin's `x-litespeed-cache: hit`. Logged-in and WooCommerce-cart cookies got `DYNAMIC`, so the rule bypasses those correctly.
- On one site, 1.3.163's "Load Simple Cloudflare Turnstile when a form comes near" (#1292) had been installed and LiteSpeed's own cached copy already had the new markup, but Cloudflare still served the copy from before the update. PageSpeed mobile: 76, LCP 5.9 s. After purging the Cloudflare zone and changing nothing else: **98, LCP 2.0 s**.
- LiteSpeed Cache's Cloudflare connection (CDN → Cloudflare API) was not set on any of these sites. With it set and **Clear Cloudflare cache** on, every Purge All also purges the zone (`src/purge.cls.php` `_purge_all()` → `CDN\Cloudflare::purge_all()`). It takes a scoped API token (Bearer) as well as the Global API Key.

## Change

1. **Hosting needs**: `cdn_probe()` in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php` (lines 1168-1204) already asks for the home page's headers. Keep `cf-cache-status` as a fact too. When it shows Cloudflare keeps the page (HIT, MISS, EXPIRED, REVALIDATED, STALE or UPDATING, not DYNAMIC or BYPASS) and LiteSpeed Cache is active without `litespeed.conf.cdn-cloudflare` and `litespeed.conf.cdn-cloudflare_clear` both on, warn: Cloudflare keeps copies of this site's pages, and nothing here clears them when LiteSpeed Cache purges. Give the steps: create a Cloudflare API token limited to Zone → Cache Purge for this zone, enter it in LiteSpeed Cache → CDN → Cloudflare API, and turn on Clear Cloudflare cache. If the site has no Cache Rule for HTML, nothing changes. Where the home page answers 403 from the server itself (#1299), keep the fact unknown; do not warn.
2. **LiteSpeed Cache preset** (`presets/litespeed-cache.json`): when the Cloudflare API is connected (`cdn-cloudflare` on, with a key and zone), turn **Clear Cloudflare cache** on, so plugin and theme updates (which the preset already makes purge everything) clear Cloudflare too. Never set a key or zone from the preset. Add a line to its notes.
3. README.md (Hosting needs) and the setting text: one sentence each.

Out of scope (owner's rule: no page caching in SEO Pro Stack): purging single pages at Cloudflare when a post is edited. Cloudflare's own plugin with APO does that. After this change, edits still wait for the edge TTL, and the Hosting needs text says so.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`: `facts()`, `cdn_probe()`, a new check next to the CDN one.
- `presets/litespeed-cache.json`
- `README.md`

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- On a LiteSpeed test site behind a Cloudflare Cache Rule that caches HTML, Hosting needs shows the new warning. With the token entered and Clear Cloudflare cache on, it clears. Applying the preset turns Clear Cloudflare cache on and leaves the key and zone as they were.
- After a plugin update on that site, the home page answers `cf-cache-status: MISS` (not a HIT with an `age` from before the update).
- A site without Cloudflare, and one where Cloudflare answers `DYNAMIC`: no warning.

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`
- `presets/litespeed-cache.json`
- `README.md`

title: Deploy: purge Cloudflare for updated sites when given a cache-purge token; warn when Cloudflare still serves pre-deploy pages
body:
## What

`scripts/deploy-sites.sh` purges each updated site's LiteSpeed cache (`load_code()` in `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`, lines 453-489), but not Cloudflare's. Where a Cloudflare Cache Rule caches HTML, visitors keep the pre-deploy pages for up to the edge TTL (2 hours by default), and the deploy reports `ok`. On 6 November 2026, after the 1.3.163 rollout, a site's home page was still served from Cloudflare with `age: 6308`, without the release's change. PageSpeed mobile went from 76 to 98 (LCP 5.9 s to 2.0 s) once the zone was purged. Nothing else changed.

The deploy's home check (#1299) fetches with `?deploy-check=`, so it never sees the cached plain address and cannot notice this.

## Fix

1. After a host's installs are applied, purge Cloudflare for each updated site, but only when the person running the deploy supplies a token. Add an option such as `--cloudflare-token-env NAME`, naming an environment variable that holds a token limited to Zone → Cache Purge. Look up each site's zone from its host name (`GET /zones?name=`, trying the registrable domain), then `POST /zones/{id}/purge_cache` with `{"purge_everything":true}`, once per zone. Never print or log the token. Run this locally, not on the host, so the token never reaches the server.
2. Report it per site on the install line (`cdn=purged`, `cdn=failed <message>`, or `cdn=-` without a token), and in the summary.
3. Without the option, check the plain home address once after the purge. When it answers `cf-cache-status: HIT` with an `age` older than the deploy, warn: `WARN Cloudflare keeps pages from before the deploy (age=N s); purge the zone or pass --cloudflare-token-env`.
4. `RELEASING.md` deploy section: the option, the token's scope, and the warning.

## Files

- `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`: the option, the local purge after each host's run, and the summary.
- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: the plain-address check (with #1299's origin pin, this needs a separate request through DNS).
- `RELEASING.md`

These are core files, so make the change in the starter as well (`STANDARDS.md` → Agent docs; the current drift is #1290).

## Verification

- ShellCheck on both scripts: no findings.
- Dry run (`--dry-run`) with the option: lists the zones it would purge and purges nothing.
- A real deploy to a site behind a Cloudflare HTML Cache Rule: the install line shows `cdn=purged`, and the home page then answers `cf-cache-status: MISS` or a `HIT` with a small `age`.
- Without the option, on the same site: the warning appears.

### Files Scope

- `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`
- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`
- `RELEASING.md`

title: Deploy: swap the plugin folder by rename, so running jobs never find it missing
body:
## What happened

During a fleet deploy of 1.3.163 (6 November 2026), one install was counted FAIL because a background job on that site crashed while the plugin folder was being replaced:

```
SEO Pro Directory import unexpected failure: … Failed opening required '…/wp-content/plugins/seoprostack/includes/image-editors/class-seoprostack-watermark-gd.php' … file=…/includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php:789
```

The import job was already running (with SEO Pro Stack loaded from the old version), lazily required a class file at the moment `wp plugin install <zip> --force` had deleted the old folder and not yet moved the new one in. The import recovered on its next part, so no data was lost, but any long-running request (imports, Action Scheduler, cron over the CLI, a slow page) can hit the same gap.

## Cause

`scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` `apply_one()` (~line 769) installs with `active_guard … plugin install "$zip" --force`. WordPress's `Plugin_Upgrader` with `clear_destination` deletes `wp-content/plugins/seoprostack/` first and then moves the unpacked copy in, so the folder is missing or partly deleted for the length of the delete plus the move (seconds on shared hosting with about 1,000 files).

## Proposed fix

Make the swap two renames inside `wp-content/plugins/` (same filesystem, so `rename()` is atomic):

1. Unpack the verified zip into a hidden sibling, for example `wp-content/plugins/.seoprostack-new-<stamp>/seoprostack/`.
2. `mv seoprostack .seoprostack-old-<stamp>` then `mv .seoprostack-new-<stamp>/seoprostack seoprostack` (the gap is two `rename()` calls).
3. Remove the old copy after the checks pass; the existing tar backup and restore line stay as they are.

Keep what `install --force` gives today: activation and network activation are kept (the folder name and main file do not change), and `check_sites()` still loads each site after the swap, which runs the settings upgrade. If the deploy relies on `upgrader_process_complete` anywhere, call the same code explicitly or keep `install --force` as a fallback when the rename fails (for example a different filesystem).

### Files Scope

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`
- `DEVELOPMENT.md`

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh shell` (ShellCheck clean).
- On a test site (`scripts/test-site.sh up`), run a loop that requests a page every 50 ms and checks the plugin folder exists, then deploy a new build to it with `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`: no request sees the folder missing, the plugin stays active (and network active on `--multisite`), and the version changes.
- A deploy to one live install reports `ok` and leaves no `.seoprostack-new-*` or `.seoprostack-old-*` folder behind.

title: Speed: load jQuery at the end of the page when nothing in the head needs it
body:
## What

WordPress registers `jquery-core` and `jquery-migrate` in the head group, and a script's dependencies print no later than the script. So when a footer script that needs jQuery is enqueued before `wp_head`, jQuery and jQuery Migrate print in the head as synchronous, render-blocking scripts (about 30 KB plus Migrate), even though nothing in the head needs them.

The Kadence theme does this on every shop: `kadence-shop-spinner` (footer, depends on `jquery`) is enqueued with WooCommerce active. PropertyHive's footer scripts do the same.

## Evidence (6 November 2026, Kadence sites on Hostinger, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.163)

- PageSpeed Insights (mobile) on a Kadence + WooCommerce site after Used CSS: performance 99, FCP 1.8 s; the largest render-blocking request left is `wp-includes/js/jquery/jquery.min.js` (est. 601 ms, 30.5 KB).
- A read-only WP-CLI probe of the queued scripts on that home page found only `kadence-shop-spinner` (group 1, deps `jquery`) needing jQuery; on a second site, three PropertyHive footer scripts.
- HTML survey of 17 fleet home pages: jQuery in the head on 5. Of those, 3 have no head script that needs jQuery; 2 have head scripts that do (Bookly, AffiliateWP, a legacy theme), so they must stay as they are. Most Kadence sites already print jQuery in the footer, because their forms enqueue it while the content renders.

## How

New Speed feature **Load jQuery at the end of the page** (`jquery_footer`, on by default, in the Recommended speed settings), `includes/features/class-seoprostack-jquery-footer.php`:

1. At `wp_head` priority 8 (after `wp_print_styles`, before `wp_print_head_scripts` at 9), on visitor page views (not logged in, feeds, embeds, the Customizer, AJAX, REST, previews, or the WooCommerce cart, checkout or account), and only when `jquery-core` is core's file and is already needed by the queue: set `group` 1 on `jquery`, `jquery-core` and `jquery-migrate`, and print the marker `<!--seoprostack-jquery-->`. WordPress's own dependency order then keeps jQuery in the head if any head script declares it, and otherwise prints it in the footer just before its first dependent.
2. An output buffer (template_redirect, `PHP_INT_MAX`, like Delay scripts) does nothing without the marker. If jQuery printed in the body, it checks everything between the marker and jQuery. It moves jQuery's tags (`jquery-core-js`, `jquery-migrate-js`, `jquery-js` and their `-extra`, `-before`, `-after` and `-translations` inline scripts, in order) back to the marker, where WordPress would have printed them, when it finds any of these:
   - an inline script (other than `seoprostack/delayed`) whose code mentions `jQuery`, or a Google Tag Manager container (`googletagmanager.com/gtm.js`, whose custom HTML tags may use jQuery);
   - a script file on this site that is not `defer` or a module, and not in WordPress's `wp-includes`, the Kadence theme (or its child), SEO Pro Stack, or the plugins Used CSS handles (`SEOProStack_Used_Css_Links::PLUGINS`) plus the other recommended plugins with front-end scripts (Burst Statistics, SEO Pro Cookie Consent, SEO Pro Analytics);
   - a synchronous script on another site (`async`, `defer`, modules and non-JavaScript types such as consent-blocked `text/plain` are fine).
3. The marker is always removed. Filter `seoprostack_jquery_footer` (bool, default true) per page.

Not in scope: deferring jQuery or its dependents. Inline scripts would break.

## Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-jquery-footer.php`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-links.php`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-speed-plan.php`
- `README.md`
- `changelog.txt`

## Acceptance

- On a test site (Kadence, WooCommerce, Fluent Forms): the home page prints jQuery after `</head>`, just before `kadence-shop-spinner`; a form page still works (submission, validation errors); the add-to-cart spinner works.
- With a raw inline `<script>jQuery(function(){})</script>` in the content, jQuery prints in the head, at the marker's place, and the console has no errors.
- With a head script that depends on `jquery`, nothing changes.
- With the setting off, or for a logged-in user, the page prints as before.
- PHP lint, PHPCS and PHPStan as in CI.
- Live: on the Kadence + WooCommerce site, PSI no longer lists `jquery.min.js` as render-blocking, and screenshots of the home, a form page and a product page match the pages without it.

title: Image loading: a Kadence Blocks Pro Advanced Slider loads only the first slide's picture with the page, preloaded
body:
## What

Image loading: on a page with a Kadence Blocks Pro **Advanced Slider** (`kadence/slider`), only the first slide's background picture loads with the page; each other slide's picture loads when Splide makes it the next (or a visible) slide. When the page opens with the slider, its first slide's picture is preloaded at high priority in the head, as a Kadence row's background already is.

## Why (measured)

A home page that opens with a 17-slide Advanced Slider (fade, loop, autoplay every 3 s, each slide a 2,500 px upload), Kadence theme, LiteSpeed Cache, Used CSS on, nothing render-blocking left:

- PageSpeed mobile 75, LCP 15.3 s (desktop 85, LCP 2.8 s); the LCP element is the first slide's `.kb-advanced-slide-inner-wrap`.
- 28 images, 4.9 MB of the page's 5.4 MB; the slides' pictures are most of it, all fetched at once at low priority, competing with the first slide's.
- A second site with the same slider: 29 images, 4.5 MB.

Why every slide loads: Kadence Blocks Pro 2.9.0 writes each slide's picture into the block's CSS (`.wp-block-kadence-slider .kb-slide-<id> .kb-advanced-slide-inner-wrap { background-image: url(...) }`, `includes/blocks/class-kadence-blocks-pro-slide-block.php`), and Splide keeps every slide rendered (stacked at opacity 0 in fade mode, off-screen in carousels), so browsers fetch every slide's background straight away. The first slide's picture is found only once that CSS has been applied, so it is also found late (resource load delay 0.25–1 s observed).

## How

1. `SEOProStack_Image_Loading::kadence_preload()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php` ~166): when the content opens with `kadence/slider` whose first inner block is a `kadence/slide` with `backgroundImg[0].img`, a normal background type and no `backgroundGradient` (Kadence's `switch` falls through to the gradient, which then replaces the picture), preload that picture (`SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images::first_copy()`) with `fetchpriority="high"`, and count it as the page's one high-priority picture, as for a row.
2. New `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-slider.php`, from `render_block_kadence/slider` on the front end: before each slider, a style and a one-line script (`SEOProStack_Kadence_Hero::SCRIPT_ATTRS`, so optimisers leave it alone). The script adds a class to `<html>`; under it, every slide's `.kb-advanced-slide-inner-wrap` except the first slide's (by its `kb-slide-<uniqueID>` class, so loop clones of it keep it too) has `background-image: none` until Splide gives its `li.splide__slide` `is-active`, `is-next`, `is-prev` or `is-visible`. The next slide's picture then starts loading one autoplay interval before it shows.
3. Fail-safe: once the page has loaded, if no slide of the slider has `is-active` (Splide not started, or renamed its classes), the class is removed and every slide's picture loads as before. Without JavaScript nothing is hidden.
4. Filter `seoprostack_kadence_slider_wait` (default true, with the block) to turn it off; README.md Image loading section and filter list; changelog `= Unreleased =`.

title: Hreflang: TranslatePress codes use the site's own country, plus language-only codes
body:
## Task

TranslatePress hreflang codes: use the site's own country for every language, plus the language-only codes.

## Why

TranslatePress derives each hreflang code from the WordPress locale. A regional site that uses `fr_FR` for its French pages therefore says `hreflang="fr-FR"`, telling search engines the page is for France. Observed on a network of regional directory sites (6 November 2026):

- A Jersey site: `en-GB`, `fr-FR`, `pt-PT`, `pl-PL`, `ro-RO`.
- US sites: `es-MX`.
- Belgian and German sites: `en-GB` for their English pages.

The language-only codes (`en`, `fr`, `es`) are present too, so the pages still match their languages, but the country signal is wrong. Wanted: the site's own country (`en-JE`, `fr-JE`, `es-US`, `en-BE`) plus the language-only codes.

## How

- New feature `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hreflang-country.php` (like `class-seoprostack-translatepress-colours.php`), setting `hreflang_country`: a two-letter ISO 3166-1 code, empty by default (off).
- When it is set and TranslatePress is active, filter `trp_hreflang` (priority after TranslatePress's own ISO fix at 10): a code with a region (`fr-FR`) becomes language + site country (`fr-JE`). Language-only codes are unchanged. TranslatePress applies the same filter to `<head>` links and to its SEO Pack sitemap `xhtml:link` entries, so both change together.
- A locale without a region (`lv`, `et`) gives TranslatePress the same input for its region and language-only calls, so it keeps only the language-only code. That carries no wrong country.
- README and changelog.

## Acceptance

- With `hreflang_country` = `JE` on a TranslatePress site: `hreflang="fr-JE"` and `hreflang="fr"` both point to `/fr/`, and there is no `fr-FR`. The sitemap shows the same codes.
- With an empty setting, the output is identical to before.
- Without TranslatePress, nothing is added.

## Verification

Repo PHPCS/PHPStan; after release, `curl` a regional page and its `page-sitemap.xml` and compare the hreflang codes.

title: Keep pages cached: warm the WebP copy of each page that browsers get
body:
## What happens

Keep pages cached asks for each page with `Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml`
(`includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php:237`). Both page caches SEO Pro
Stack works with keep a separate copy of each page for browsers that accept WebP when
their WebP option is on:

- LiteSpeed Cache with WebP replacement on (`img_optm-webp`) adds `+webp` to the cache
  vary when the `Accept` header holds `image/webp` (or the user agent is Lighthouse,
  Googlebot, iPhone OS 14+, Safari 16.4+ on a Mac, or Firefox 65+); see the
  `### marker WEBP` block it writes to `.htaccess`.
- WP-Optimize with WebP images on (not its redirect method) saves the page as
  `<file>.webp` when the `Accept` header holds `image/webp`
  (`cache/file-based-page-cache-functions.php`, `wpo_is_browser_supports_webp()`).

Every current browser sends `image/webp` (and `image/avif`) when it opens a page. So:

- On LiteSpeed, the desktop copy Keep pages cached warms is one no desktop browser
  gets. Its phone request still gets the WebP copy, because its iPhone user agent
  matches LiteSpeed's rule.
- On WP-Optimize, neither the desktop copy nor the phone copy it warms is the one browsers get.

## Evidence (2026-11-06, Hostinger origin, Server IP pinned, 1.3.166)

A site on a multisite network (LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1, WebP replacement on network-wide),
after Keep pages cached had filled the site:

```text
browser=miss  warmer-copy=hit   https://<site>/cookies/
browser=miss  warmer-copy=hit   https://<site>/about/
browser=miss  warmer-copy=hit   https://<site>/<service-page>/
... 10 of 11 linked pages: miss for desktop Chrome's Accept, hit for the warmer's
```

`browser` = desktop Chrome's `Accept`
(`text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,image/avif,image/webp,image/apng,*/*;q=0.8`);
`warmer-copy` = the warmer's. Only the home page was a hit for both: a browser-style
request had opened it earlier.

LiteSpeed Cache's own crawler does the same as the fix below: with WebP replacement on it
crawls with `Accept: image/webp,*/*` (`image/avif` when set to AVIF) and skips the plain
copy unless the `litespeed_crawler_webp` filter asks for it (`src/crawler.cls.php` ~469, ~1270).

## Fix

`SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::request()` sends the `Accept` header a browser sends
when it opens a page (Chrome's, which lists `image/avif` and `image/webp`), for both the
desktop and phone requests and for `page_html()`. Where no WebP copy is kept, the page
cache ignores `Accept`, so the same single copy is warmed as before. Do not also warm the
plain copy: no current browser gets it, and it would double the requests.

Files: `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php` (`request()`, constant for
the header). Changelog entries in `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, `README.md` (Unreleased).

## Verify

1. `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
2. On a LiteSpeed site with WebP replacement on: purge, let Keep pages cached run
   (`wp seoprostack keep-cached` or its cron), then from outside with the origin pinned,
   desktop Chrome's `Accept` gets `x-litespeed-cache: hit` for the warmed pages.
3. No PHP messages in the site's log.

body:
## What happens With LiteSpeed Cache's WebP replacement on (`img_optm-webp`), the first slide's picture of a Kadence Blocks Pro Advanced Slider (GH#1312), and a hero row's picture when it has no smaller copies (GH#1204), download twice at high priority. - `SEOProStack_Image_Loading::preload()` prints `` in the head. - At the end of the page, LiteSpeed Cache's `Media::finalize()` (`litespeed_buffer_finalize`, priority 4) rewrites every CSS `url()` whose picture has a WebP (or AVIF) file to `…/picture.jpg.webp` (`replace_background_webp()`), including the slide's and the row's CSS from Kadence. It rewrites `` attributes and `srcset`, but not a `` href. - So the browser fetches the preloaded `.jpg`, then finds the slide's `.jpg.webp` only after the CSS, and that one is the LCP picture: the preload is wasted and the picture comes twice. LiteSpeed rewrites only on pages it caches, for browsers that get its WebP copy (`Accept` with `image/webp`, or Lighthouse, Googlebot, iPhone OS 14+, Safari 16.4+ on a Mac, Firefox 65+). So the preload must follow what LiteSpeed did on that request, not guess it when the head is printed. ## Evidence (PageSpeed mobile, 6 November 2026, 1.3.166, a Kadence home page opening with a 17-slide Advanced Slider) ```text 256 ms 214 KiB High …/2025/04/.jpg (SEO Pro Stack's preload) 353 ms 214 KiB High …/2025/04/.jpg.webp (the slide's CSS, rewritten by LiteSpeed; the LCP) LCP subparts (observed): TTFB 49 ms, resource load delay 303 ms, load 151 ms, render delay 216 ms ``` Mobile score 76, LCP 7.5 s (simulated); before 1.3.166 it was 69 and 16.4 s. ## Fix In `includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`: - `preload()` keeps the address and tag it printed when no SEO Pro Stack copy was used (`SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images::first_copy()` gave no type). - When LiteSpeed Cache is active, a `litespeed_buffer_after` filter swaps the preload's href for `
.avif` or `

Otherwise the page is left alone. - No change when SEO Pro Stack's own copies are named (the CSS then names them too), or for the hero sizing script (GH#1221), which sets the row's picture and its preload to the same address. ## Verify 1. `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`. 2. title: Image loading: Kadence row backgrounds below the first screen wait until the visitor scrolls near them
body: ## What happens A Kadence Blocks row's background picture is in the page's CSS (`.kb-row-layout-id{background-image:url(…)}`), so browsers fetch it as soon as the row is laid out, wherever the row is on the page. Rows further down a home page fetch their full-size pictures with the page and compete with the first screen's picture (LCP) on a phone. Image loading already handles the first row (GH#1204, GH#1221) and Advanced Slider slides (GH#1312), and `` tags get the browser's own lazy loading; rows below the first screen get nothing. ## Evidence (6 November 2026, 1.3.166, PageSpeed mobile) On a Kadence home page opening with an Advanced Slider: a row further down (`kb-row-layout-id315_…`) fetched its 566 KiB WebP background at 364 ms, Low priority, before the first slide was painted (mobile 76, LCP 7.5 s simulated, 2,547 KiB in all). Kadence row backgrounds on the measured home pages (`row-bg-count`): three sites have a second row with a background picture (741 KiB, 633 KiB and 1,591 KiB for both rows). Kadence Blocks 3.9's own Performance Optimizer has a background lazy loader (`includes/resources/Optimizer/Lazy_Load/Background_Lazy_Loader.php`), but it is off unless `performance_optimizer_enabled`, needs its in-browser analysis of each page, and removes the row's whole `class` attribute until the row is in view. ## Proposal Same pattern as `SEOProStack_Kadence_Slider` (GH#1312), Kadence only, no page rewriting: - `render_block_kadence/rowlayout` on front-end pages: for a row that is not the content's first block, has a normal background picture (`bgImg`), is not parallax (`bgImgAttachment` parallax / `kt-jarallax`), has no background slider or video, and has no `data-kadence-lazy-class` (Kadence's optimizer handles that one), add before it a style `html.sps-rows .kb-row-layout-id:not(.sps-near){background-image:none!important}` and, once a page, a small script (`SEOProStack_Kadence_Hero::SCRIPT_ATTRS`) that adds `sps-rows` to `` only when `IntersectionObserver` exists, and adds `sps-near` to each such row when it comes within one screen of the viewport (`rootMargin` 100%). - Without JavaScript, or a browser without IntersectionObserver, nothing waits. Rows on the first screen get `sps-near` at the observer's first callback. - Filter `seoprostack_kadence_row_wait` (default true), as `seoprostack_kadence_slider_wait`. - Unique IDs limited to letters, digits, `-` and `_` (as the slider and hero do). Files: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php` (`boot()`), new `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-rows.php` (model: `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-slider.php`), changelogs. ## Verify 1. `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`. 2. Test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`) with Kadence Blocks and a page whose second and third rows have background pictures: phone-sized browser, throttled; the rows' pictures are requested only on scrolling near them; a row on the first screen shows its picture; no layout shift; no console errors; without JavaScript every picture shows. 3. Live: PageSpeed mobile on the home page above: the 566 KiB request gone from the page load, LCP lower; screenshots match before and after. --- [aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.39.131 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.19.5 with claude-opus-5-5 spent 2d 22h and 5,281,360 tokens on this with the user in an interactive session.

title: Advanced Slider's script stops curly quotes in the rest of the post content
body:
## What happens SEO Pro Stack 1.3.166 (GH#1312) prints a script just before a Kadence Blocks Pro Advanced Slider, inside the post content (`render_block_kadence/slider`, `SEOProStack_Kadence_Slider::script()` in `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-slider.php`). The script has a `<` in it (`for (i = 0; i < s.length; i++)`). `wptexturize()` runs on the post content after the blocks are rendered. It splits the content on anything that starts with `<`, so it reads `< s.length; ...` as one HTML tag. Two things follow: - Every `&` from that `<` to the next `>` becomes `&`. The slider's script has no `&` after its `<`, so it still works. A script with `&&` after a `<` breaks with `SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token`, which is what happened to the first draft of #1329's script. - The real `` is swallowed by that false tag, so `script` stays on wptexturize's stack of tags it leaves alone. The rest of the post content after the slider gets no curly quotes, dashes or ellipses, up to the next `` in the content. ## Evidence Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3): ``` wp eval 'echo wptexturize("

\"a\"

\"after\"

");'

“a”

"after"

``` On two live Kadence sites whose home pages open with an Advanced Slider, the home page and an inner page have no curly quotes at all (6 November 2026, 1.3.166). This fits the bug but does not prove it, as no page without the slider was compared. ## Fix Scripts SEO Pro Stack prints in post content carry no `<`: loop with `Array.prototype.forEach.call()` instead. Say why in the docblock, so later edits keep it. The hero's one-line row script (`window.seoprostackHero&&seoprostackHero(...)`) has no `<` and is unaffected. Scripts printed in the head, footer or through `script_loader_tag` do not pass through `wptexturize()`. Files: `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-slider.php` (`script()`), and the new `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-rows.php` from #1329. ## Verification - A `wp eval-file` check that runs each script through `wptexturize()` between two quoted paragraphs: the script comes out unchanged, and the text after it gets curly quotes. - Test site page with Kadence rows and a paragraph with straight quotes after them: curly quotes in the page, no console errors. - `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`. --- [aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.39.131 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.19.5 with claude-opus-5-5 spent 2d 22h and 5,319,256 tokens on this with the user in an interactive session.

title: Advanced Slider slides at the size each screen needs
body:
## What

Kadence Blocks Pro Advanced Slider slides name the picture's full upload, so phones get it. Give each slide's picture at the size the screen needs, as #1221 does for the row a page opens with, and never less sharp than now.

## Evidence

On one Kadence home page (`<site>`) opening with a 17-slide Advanced Slider (6 November 2026, 1.3.166), tested on a throttled phone (Playwright, 412×823, DPR 1.75):

- The slides' CSS names files such as `…-2500.jpg`. LiteSpeed's WebP replacement makes that `…-2500.jpg.webp`.
- #1312 fetches the next slides one slide ahead. Two of them came in at 673 KiB and 354 KiB during the page load.
- WordPress made smaller copies of the same pictures, which nothing uses. On the server, for the 673 KiB slide:

| File | Size |
|---|---|
| `…-2500.jpg` | 1,717 KiB |
| `…-2500.jpg.webp` | 672 KiB |
| `…-2500-1024x768.jpg.webp` | 141 KiB |
| `…-2500-768x576.jpg` | 108 KiB |

- There is no 1536 copy on that site, so a slide that paints more than 1,024 px across still needs the full file. Measure the slider before choosing.

## Plan

Follow the #1221 pattern (`SEOProStack_Kadence_Hero` and `SEOProStack_Hero_Picture`, `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-hero.php` and `includes/class-seoprostack-hero-picture.php`) inside `SEOProStack_Kadence_Slider` (`includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-slider.php`).

1. For each slide (`kadence/slide` inner blocks, `backgroundImg[0]` with its attachment ID), collect the attachment's sizes with the same proportions (height within a pixel). Take only files in its uploads folder or mapped by Media in cloud storage, with their AVIF and WebP copies, exactly as `SEOProStack_Hero_Picture` does.
2. Print them in the slider's existing script, without `<` (#1331). Measure the slider box and the slide's computed `background-size` once it is read.
3. For each slide, pick the smallest file at least as wide as the painted pixels × DPR × 1.1. That is the larger of the width, and the height × the picture's proportions, for `cover`. Fall back to the slide's own picture, so it is never less sharp. Set it on `.kb-advanced-slide-inner-wrap` with `!important`.
4. If the slider grows or the pixel ratio rises (ResizeObserver, `matchMedia` resolution), swap in a larger file, never a smaller one, as #1221 does.
5. The head preload of the first slide (#1312, `SEOProStack_Image_Loading::kadence_preload()`) names the chosen copy, as the hero script does. It must stay compatible with #1326 (LiteSpeed's WebP name).
6. Leave alone: slides with a gradient, `background-size` other than `cover` and `contain`, block themes, and pictures without smaller copies. Add an off switch filter.

## Verification

- Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, Kadence, Kadence Blocks 3.9.0, Kadence Blocks Pro 2.9.0) with a slider of 2048×1536 uploads that have 768, 1024 and 1536 copies. Use Chromium at 412×823 DPR 1.75, 393×852 DPR 3, 768×1024 DPR 2 and 1350×940 DPR 1.
- Pass when every slide shown uses a file at least as wide as the pixels painted, one file per picture is fetched (never the full one as well as a copy), and there are no console errors.
- JavaScript off: as now.
- Run each new script through `wptexturize()`: it must come out unchanged (#1331).
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Live: the home page above on PageSpeed mobile (keyed). Compare bytes and LCP with 1.3.168.

title: Image loading: preload the first Kadence slide's or hero row's copy from the head (imagesrcset), not after the CSS
body:
## What

Image loading: start fetching the first Kadence picture (the first slide of an Advanced Slider, or the background of the row a page opens with) from the head, at the size the screen needs, instead of waiting for the stylesheets.

## Why

With #1221 (hero row) and #1333 (Advanced Slider), the copy each screen needs is chosen by an inline script printed right after the row or slider. That script then preloads the copy. Browsers do not run an inline script until every stylesheet above it has loaded, so the picture's request starts only after the CSS.

Evidence: a Kadence home page that opens with a 3-slide Advanced Slider, on 1.3.169 (7 November 2026), keyed PageSpeed, mobile:
- Score 94; FCP 1.4 s; **LCP 3.1 s** (simulated 4G).
- Lighthouse LCP breakdown (observed): TTFB 36 ms, **resource load delay 349 ms**, load 157 ms, render delay 127 ms.
- LCP element: the first slide's `.kb-advanced-slide-inner-wrap`, whose picture is the 81 KiB WebP 1024 copy the script chose and preloaded.

A sister site that opens the same way scored 89 with LCP 3.6 s. Below LCP 2.5 s, mobile should reach the high 90s.

## How (proposed)

1. In `SEOProStack_Image_Loading::kadence_preload()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`), when `SEOProStack_Kadence_Slider::opens()` or `SEOProStack_Kadence_Hero::start()` takes the picture, print in the head `<link rel="preload" as="image" imagesrcset="<copies with w descriptors>" imagesizes="<estimate>" fetchpriority="high">`. Use the same copies as `SEOProStack_Hero_Picture::get()`, with each file's AVIF or WebP copy when pages name copies, as `first_copy()` does. The current `<noscript>` preload of the picture's own file stays for browsers without JavaScript.
   - `imagesizes` estimate: the painted width, i.e. the box width for `cover` when the box is wider than the picture's proportions, else box height × aspect. For a full-width slider or row, `100vw` scaled by `max(1, boxAspect / pictureAspect)` where the block's height or aspect is known. When it cannot be estimated, skip the head preload and keep today's behaviour.
2. In the size scripts (`size_script()` in `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-slider.php`, and the script in `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-hero.php`), check before choosing which candidate the browser already fetched for the head preload (`performance.getEntriesByType('resource')` names). If that file is at least `painted × devicePixelRatio` wide (no 10% margin), use it, so nothing is fetched twice. Otherwise choose as now (never less sharp) and skip the preload the script adds.
3. LiteSpeed Cache's WebP replacement does not rewrite `imagesrcset`. Either let `litespeed_next_gen()` (#1326) rewrite each candidate when the page names its `.webp` copy, or leave the head preload out on LiteSpeed's WebP pages. Measure which is better.

title: Image loading: Kadence row background slider's first slide at full width before the slider script runs (LCP)
body:
## What

Image loading: the first slide of a Kadence Blocks row background slider shows at its full width from the first paint, not only after the slider's script has run.

## Why

Kadence Blocks resets the slider list's margin and padding only under `.kb-splide`: `.kb-splide .splide__list{…;margin:0!important;padding:0!important}` (`kadence-blocks/includes/assets/css/kadence-splide.min.css`, 3.8 and 3.9). `kb-splide-init` adds `kb-splide` when Splide mounts. Until then, the `<ul class="splide__list">` keeps the browser's default 40 px left padding, so the first slide is 40 px narrower and offset to the right.

When Splide mounts, the slide widens to full width. Chrome then records a new, larger Largest Contentful Paint for the same picture, so LCP waits for `splide.min.js` and `kb-splide-init.min.js`. Those load in the footer, and with Cloudflare Rocket Loader they run only after the page has loaded.

Evidence: three Kadence home pages that open with a row background slider, on 1.3.169 (7 November 2026):
- Keyed PageSpeed, mobile: scores 85, 88 and 81; LCP 4.4 s, 3.9 s and 5.0 s.
- Lighthouse LCP breakdown (observed): element render delay 494 ms, 429 ms and 400 ms.
- Lighthouse trace for the first page: the slide's picture finished loading at 385 ms, but LCP was recorded at 880 ms, after the slider scripts ran (554–615 ms, load 597 ms).
- Playwright, phone 412×823 @1.75, throttled: the first slide is 372 px wide before Splide mounts and 412 px after. LCP entries for the same picture: 148,800 then 164,800 px² (first page); 143,964 at 2,916 ms then 151,912 at 3,320 ms (second page).

## How

In `SEOProStack_Kadence_Rows::around_row()` (`includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-rows.php`), before the first row on a front-end page whose background tab is `slider` and whose HTML holds `kb-blocks-bg-slider`, print once:

```html
<style class="seoprostack-bg-slider" data-no-optimize="1">.kb-blocks-bg-slider .splide__list{margin:0;padding:0}</style>
```

These are the values Kadence sets once the slider mounts, so nothing changes afterwards. The style has no `<` or `&` (it is printed in the post's content; #1331). Apply it to every row background slider, not only the row the page opens with, because a slider further up the first screen can be the LCP too. Add a filter, `seoprostack_kadence_bg_slider_fix` (default true), as the other Kadence output has.

## Verification

- Test site with Kadence and Kadence Blocks (free is enough), a page that opens with a row background slider (fade, 2 slides). Phone 412×823 @1.75: the first slide's width before Splide mounts equals its width after, and there is one LCP entry for the picture, not two. The slider still fades and the dots work.
- Same with a row background slider as the second row.
- `wptexturize()` leaves the style unchanged (the #1331 check).
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Live: keyed PageSpeed mobile on the three home pages. Report LCP and element render delay before and after.

title: Image loading: every Kadence row and column background at the size the screen needs
body:
## What

Image loading: give every Kadence Blocks row and column background picture at the size the screen needs, not only the row a page opens with (#1221) and Advanced Slider slides (#1333).

## Why

Kadence Blocks writes the picture a row or column names, usually the full upload, into the page's CSS. Phones get the whole file even where it paints a small box.

Evidence: one Kadence home page on 1.3.169 (7 November 2026), keyed PageSpeed mobile, score 83, LCP 4.8 s:
- LCP element: a Kadence column's `.kt-inside-inner-col` background. The picture is the 1365×1024 upload, served as AVIF, **293 KiB**, painting a 126×189 box. Lighthouse's observed load duration was 764 ms.
- Two more column backgrounds: 1929×1454 (134 KiB) for 150×106, and 1800×1365 (85 KiB) for 114×76.
- Lighthouse's image delivery insight puts the waste at 289 + 134 + 84 KiB.

A second Kadence home page on 1.3.166 had a row about 30,000 px down on a phone with a 566 KiB full-size background (#1329 now holds it until near, but it is still the full file).

## How (proposed)

Reuse the size-picking from `SEOProStack_Kadence_Hero` (`includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-hero.php`) and #1329's IntersectionObserver in `SEOProStack_Kadence_Rows` (`includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-rows.php`):

1. Around each Kadence row (`render_block_kadence/rowlayout`) and column (`render_block_kadence/column`) whose normal background is a picture with smaller copies (`SEOProStack_Hero_Picture::get()`), background size `cover`, `contain` or unset, and no parallax, print the copies list once in the row's existing style or one-line script.
2. When the row or column comes near (#1329's `sps-near`, 1,250 px), the script measures its box, as `need()` and `pick()` do, and sets the narrowest copy at least `painted × devicePixelRatio × 1.1` as an inline `background-image` with `!important`. It grows on ResizeObserver; never smaller.
3. Columns: Kadence column backgrounds sit on `.kadence-column<id> > .kt-inside-inner-col`. Each needs the same hide-until-sized rule, under `html.sps-rows`, so the full file is not fetched as well.
4. Tablet and phone backgrounds of their own, gradients, dynamic and parallax backgrounds: left as now. Without JavaScript: the row's or column's own picture, as now.
5. LiteSpeed Cache WebP replacement: name each file as `url(…)` in the script data, as #1333's `SEOProStack_Hero_Picture::for_script()` does, so LiteSpeed rewrites it.

## Verification

- Test site with Kadence and Kadence Blocks (free): a page with a row background lower down and three columns with backgrounds in a row.
- Phone 412×823 @1.75 and desktop 1350×940: each picture fetched once, at a copy no smaller than its painted pixels × DPR; nothing fetched before the row is near; JavaScript off shows the own files.

title: Image loading: size Kadence background pictures that have no attachment ID
body:
## What

Image loading: size Kadence row, column and slide background pictures that name their picture by address only (no attachment ID), as it already does for those with an ID.

## Why

`SEOProStack_Hero_Picture::get($id, $url)` (`includes/class-seoprostack-hero-picture.php`) returns null when `$id` is 0: `meta()` needs an attachment ID. Kadence Blocks rows saved from imported templates, or with a picture pasted by address, often have `bgImg` but no `bgImgID`. Those pictures then keep the full upload:

- the row a page opens with (#1221, `SEOProStack_Kadence_Hero`) and its head preload (#1337, `SEOProStack_Kadence_Early`);
- rows and columns further down (#1341, `SEOProStack_Kadence_Rows`);
- Advanced Slider slides (#1333, `SEOProStack_Kadence_Slider`).

Live, 1.3.171, 7 November 2026: of the 7 row or column pictures below the first screen on our 13 Kadence home pages, 4 have no `bgImgID` (on 3 sites). `attachment_url_to_postid()` finds the attachment for every one, each with 3 to 5 smaller copies of the same proportions. Those 4 now wait until near (#1329) but still come as full uploads (one is a `-scaled` 2560 px picture).

## How

In `SEOProStack_Hero_Picture::get()`: when the ID is not a positive number and the address can go in CSS (`css_url()`), look the attachment up with `attachment_url_to_postid()`. Then go on as now: `meta()` still checks the address is in the attachment's folder, `named()` its size.

- `attachment_url_to_postid()` matches only this site's uploads address of the original (or `-scaled`) file, so CDN or cloud storage addresses and size copies stay as now (null).
- One query per picture on a page built by PHP; cache the result per address in the object cache (group `seoprostack`), with a 0 kept too, so a cached miss costs nothing.
- Every caller benefits; no caller changes.

Files: `includes/class-seoprostack-hero-picture.php`; docs in `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (Unreleased).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Test site: a Kadence row lower on a page with `bgImg` and no `bgImgID` gets `seoprostackRows(…,{…})` with its copies; a first row without `bgImgID` gets the hero's sizes and head script; an address outside uploads stays unsized.
- Live after release: the 4 pictures above get picture lists in their `seoprostackRows` calls (count with a phone request), and keyed PageSpeed mobile on those 3 home pages before and after.

title: Deploy check: seoprostack_front_verify cron race fails a network rollout; find the second runner
body:
## What

Two of the last three rollouts to one 11-site network install (1.3.169 and 1.3.171) ended `FAIL` with `new_log_lines=2`, although every site was on the new version, active, with every cron event run and its home page answering 200. Both times the two lines were core's cron race for `seoprostack_front_verify`, in the same second:

```
Cron reschedule event error for hook: seoprostack_front_verify, Error code: could_not_set, Error message: The cron event list could not be saved., Data: {"schedule":"seoprostack_front_verify","args":[],"interval":180}
Cron unschedule event error for hook: seoprostack_front_verify, Error code: could_not_set, ...
```

#1300 forgives this race only for hooks `run_site_cron()` ran itself (`CRON_HOOKS_RUN` in `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`). `seoprostack_front_verify` was not among them on any site, so the line failed the install.

## Evidence (point-in-time, 7 November 2026)

- Both `front_verify` races are inside the two deploys' windows (01:17:05 and 04:47:17 UTC); none outside them in the network's web PHP log since 31 October.
- Both lines failing together means another process had already rescheduled the same event from the same time: two runners handled it in the same second.
- The network's WP-Cron is off (`DISABLE_WP_CRON`). Its scheduled runner holds a per-network `flock` and runs core's `wp-cron.php` per site (core's per-site lock). The deploy's `wp cron event run` calls take no lock but did not run this hook. The second runner is not identified.
- `seoprostack_front_verify` repeats every 180 s only while addresses wait (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::schedule_verify()`, `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php` ~L1036). The deploy's home fetches queue addresses (`queue_page()`), so the event is due during deploys, which may be why it races only then.
- The same log has 58 other `could_not_set` lines since 31 October, outside deploys, for other hooks: AI Engine `mwai_tasks_internal_run` (26), `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached` (11, unschedule only), Action Scheduler, MainWP and Link Whisper hooks. So overlapping runs on this network happen beyond deploys too.

## To do

1. Find the second runner: during a deploy of the network, log each process that runs `seoprostack_front_verify` (PID, `PHP_SAPI`, `DOING_CRON`, `WP_CLI`, the request), for example with a temporary must-use file. Remove it afterwards.
2. If the deploy causes it (its own processes), add `seoprostack_front_verify` to the hooks the race check forgives, or have `run_site_cron()` list it.
3. If the host's runner overlaps with itself or with core's lock, report it against that runner and leave the deploy gate strict.
4. `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached` unschedule-only errors: check whether a purge inside a cron run moves the fill (`wp_clear_scheduled_hook()` then a later time) while core's run still holds the old list, so core finds it gone and **still runs the fill** from its stale list. If so, the fill runs early despite being moved back. Fix in `SEOProStack_Keep_Pages_Cached` if confirmed.

## Files

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: `classify_log()` (~L401), `run_site_cron()` (~L614), `cron_list_code()` (~L562). Core file: change the starter as well (`STANDARDS.md` → Agent docs).
- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: `schedule_verify()`, `clear_verify()`, `keep_in_cron()` (~L1036–1092).
- The Keep pages cached class for step 4 (path not checked; find it with `rg -n "seoprostack_keep_pages_cached'" includes/`).

## Verification

- A deploy of the network ends `ok`, or `WARN cron race seoprostack_front_verify` when the deploy is shown to cause it.
- ShellCheck on `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: no findings.
- For step 4: a purge inside a cron run leaves the fill at its new time and does not run it at once.

title: Deploy: OPcache keeps the old code after a rollout (zip file times), so a network purges its page cache on every request
body:
## What

After a rollout with `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`, a multisite network's web requests kept running the **previous** version's PHP code for hours, while WP-CLI and the files on disk were on the new one. On every request the two sides disagreed about `seoprostack_page_cache_purged` (`SEOProStack_Page_Cache::after_update()`), so each one purged the site's whole page cache and wrote its own version back:

- WP-CLI (and the host's cron runner, every 5 minutes) saw the old version stored → purged everything → stored the new version.
- The next uncached web request (old code) saw the new version → purged everything → stored the old version.

Pages could never stay cached on that network: Keep pages cached warmed them, and the next flip wiped them. This is the "pages too slow to be cached" seen on network subsites.

## Evidence (point-in-time, 7 November 2026, an 11-site network on LiteSpeed)

- `wp option get seoprostack_page_cache_purged` stayed `1.3.171` on every subsite after the 1.3.172 rollout; each `wp` command printed LiteSpeed's "Purged all caches successfully."
- A `litespeed_purged_all` backtrace from a WP-CLI load: `SEOProStack_Page_Cache::after_update` (class-seoprostack-page-cache.php:74) on `wp_loaded`.
- In one WP-CLI process the row read `1.3.172` at `wp_loaded` and `1.3.171` at `shutdown`, with no other write from that process: a web request wrote it back.
- Uncached web pages (unique query string, pinned to the origin) linked SEO Pro Stack's assets with `ver=1.3.171`; on a single site deployed the same way they showed `1.3.172`.
- The web pool's OPcache: `validate_timestamps=1`, `revalidate_freq=2`, started 04:29 UTC, never restarted; `seoprostack.php` on disk **and** in the cache both dated `2020-01-01T00:00:00Z`.

## Why

`scripts/build-release.sh` gives every file in the zip the fixed time 2020-01-01 (reproducible builds). `swap_plugin_folder()` in `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` extracts with `unzip`, which keeps that time. OPcache revalidates by modification time only, so it sees an unchanged file and keeps the old compiled code. (WordPress's own updater writes files with the current time, so it is not affected.)

Single sites recover after one or two extra purges because LiteSpeed Cache's purge from a web request also resets OPcache. Since LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.x, on a multisite network it does that only for a network admin, so a network never recovers by itself.

Side effect: assets versioned with `filemtime()` (form keys, form modal, brand icons, admin dark mode and others) keep `ver=1577836800` across releases, so browsers and CDNs can keep the old files after a rollout.

Remediation already done on the affected network: `touch` on the plugin's files; within 2 s the web requests ran 1.3.172 and the marker held.

## Change

1. `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` (core file): after unzipping into the staging folder, give the extracted files the current time before the swap (so OPcache revalidates them and `filemtime()` versions change). Port to the starter (wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding, with #646).
2. `SEOProStack_Page_Cache::after_update()`: purge and store only when the running code is newer than the stored version (or none is stored). A process still running older compiled code then leaves the cache and the marker alone, so the two can never alternate purges again, whatever installed the files.
3. README.md, readme.txt, changelog.txt.

## How to check

- `shellcheck -x scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh scripts/deploy-sites.sh`; `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Roll out to a single site with the fixed script: the plugin's files have the deploy's time (`stat`), and uncached pages link its assets with the new `ver=`.
- On a network: after the rollout, `wp option get seoprostack_page_cache_purged` on each site stays at the new version, and a `wp` command prints no purge message.

title: Used CSS: elements scripts create with an ID show unstyled until the full stylesheet arrives (Readabler voice panel)
body:
## What happens

With **Load the CSS each page uses first** on, an element a script creates with an ID shows unstyled until that plugin's full stylesheet arrives. Found on a network subsite with Readabler: its script (`readabler.min.js`, which runs as the page loads) builds the voice navigation panel in code:

```js
const e = "mdp-readabler-voice-navigation", t = document.createElement("div");
t.id = e, t.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true");
```

The rules that place and hide it are ID rules:

```css
#mdp-readabler-voice-navigation{position:fixed;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);bottom:0;z-index:99998}
#mdp-readabler-voice-navigation[aria-hidden=true]{display:none}
```

The served HTML has no element with that ID, and `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Match::added()` (`includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-match.php`, L164–176) never counts an ID as script-made (`if ('#' === $token[0]) return false;`), so neither rule is kept. Until `readabler.min.css` arrives, the panel and its command list (about 23,800 px tall at 1280 px wide) sit below the footer. The screenshot check (feature on, full stylesheets blocked) caught it as the desktop footer shot moving up 17 px with the panel's first button below the footer.

Classes and elements already count when they are words in the page's running scripts (`SEOProStack_Used_Css_Scripts`, #1260); IDs were left out.

## Change

1. `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Match::added()`: an `#id` the page's HTML lacks counts as present when it is a word in the page's running scripts, as classes and elements do. The scanner already collects those words (`WORDS`); no new reading.
2. Docblocks of `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Match` and `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Scripts` say IDs count too.
3. README.md (Load the CSS each page uses first), changelog.txt and readme.txt under `= Unreleased =`.

Cost, measured on the same page: at most 70 more rules, 11.9 KB before compression, from Readabler's stylesheet (93.7 KB), whose script runs at load. Scripts delayed until the visitor acts are not read, so they add nothing.

## How to check

1. `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
2. On a page with Readabler's script running at load and Used CSS on: view source; the used CSS for `readabler.min.css` includes `#mdp-readabler-voice-navigation[aria-hidden=true]{display:none}`.
3. Screenshot comparison with the full stylesheets blocked: the desktop footer shot matches the reference (no panel below the footer).
4. `SEO Pro Stack Used CSS: N stylesheets, X KB of Y KB` end comment: X grows by no more than about 12 KB on that page.

title: Keep pages cached: a fill moved by a purge during a cron run may still run early
body:
## What

On one 11-site network install (WP-Cron off, `wp-cron.php` run per site by the host's cron job), the web PHP log has `Cron unschedule event error for hook: seoprostack_keep_pages_cached, Error code: could_not_set` lines with no matching `reschedule` line: 11 between 31 October and 6 November 2026, outside deploys (latest 6 November 02:21 UTC).

An unschedule-only `could_not_set` means the event core was about to run had already gone from the stored list when core removed it, though core still ran it from the copy it read at the start (`wp-cron.php` calls the hook whatever the unschedule returned). Split out of #1349 (step 4); the deploy part of #1349 was a log-format bug, fixed in #1361.

## Hypothesis to check

A purge during a cron run moves the fill: `SEOProStack_Keep_Pages_Cached` clears the scheduled hook and schedules it at a later time ("Purges one after another … move the fill back until they stop", README.md → Keep pages cached). If that happens after core's run read its due list, core finds the old event gone (unschedule error) and **still runs the fill** from its stale list, so the fill runs early despite having been moved back.

## To do

1. Find the class and its scheduling: `rg -n "seoprostack_keep_pages_cached'" includes/`, then the code that clears and reschedules the fill on a purge.
2. Reproduce on a disposable single site with `DISABLE_WP_CRON` and `wp-cron.php` from the command line: schedule the fill due now, start `php wp-cron.php`, and from another process trigger a purge while it runs (a slow earlier event, or a `sleep` in a test-only must-use file on the disposable site). Check whether the unschedule error appears and whether the fill ran at the old time.
3. If confirmed: at the start of the fill callback, return early when the stored list (read past the caches, as `SEOProStack_Cron_List::stored()` does) has the fill at a later time than the event now running, so a moved fill is not run early. Keep the fill's own retry and back-off as they are.
4. If not confirmed, record what does cause it and close with the evidence.

## Files

- The Keep pages cached class (find it with step 1); `includes/class-seoprostack-cron-list.php` (`stored()`, the merge that leads to `could_not_set` when another request already applied a change).
- README.md → Keep pages cached, and changelog.txt / readme.txt under the next version, if behaviour changes.

## Verification

- On the disposable site, a purge during a cron run leaves the fill at its new time and does not run it at once; no `could_not_set` line for the hook.
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes (run `composer install --no-interaction --quiet` first in a fresh worktree).

body:
## Why

Owner's order for **Keep pages cached** (#1224): the header menu's links, then the footer's, then the links on the home page, then the rest of the site. Measured on live Kadence sites after the 1.3.174 deploy purge (logged out, about 45 minutes later):

- A single site whose header, footer and home page link to 80 of its pages: `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Pages::to_open()` planned 50 (`MAIN_MAX`), as LiteSpeed Cache's crawler is on (`covered()`). The other 30 (21 of the home page's own links, part of the footer) were left to the crawler, which goes in sitemap order (1,034 addresses, about 41 minutes a pass, two passes). Four of the home page's links were still uncached (1.3 to 2.3 s, against 0.1 to 0.4 s for cached pages).
- Main pages counted on eleven Kadence sites (`menu_urls()` and `page_links()`, before `clean()` drops other sites' links): 11 to 97.
- A network fill (every deploy, a network-wide purge) plans 10 main pages a site (`NETWORK_MAIN_MAX`), 25 in all (`NETWORK_MORE_MAX`), and does not read home pages (`of_site(..., false)`). Network sites with 29 to 35 header links get only the home page and the first nine header links before the crawler.

## Change

`includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-pages.php`, `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php`:

1. `MAIN_MAX` 50 → 150: every link in the header, the footer and the home page is opened first on a single site, still in that order. The crawler or WP-Optimize's preload opens these pages anyway, so this adds no page builds where one is on; it moves them before the rest.
2. A network fill goes in two rounds, so every site still gets its first pages in one round (#1240): round 1 as now but main pages only (`of_site(NETWORK_MAIN_MAX, NETWORK_MAIN_MAX, false)`: home page and first header links); round 2 each site's whole main set with its home page read (`of_site(MAIN_MAX, NETWORK_MORE_MAX, true)`), less what round 1 planned. The queue keeps the round (`round`, reset to 1 by `fill_later()` for a network fill). The capacity check in `network()` uses the round's most per site, so a site's list is never cut by `MAX`.
3. Docs: README.md, readme.txt, changelog.txt (Unreleased), and any setting text naming 50.

## How to check

1. `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
2. On a single site with LiteSpeed Cache's crawler on: `wp eval` `count(SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Pages::to_open(false))` equals the header, footer and home page links (above 50 where there are more), in that order.
3. On a network: after `wp litespeed-purge all`, the queue plans every site's first pages, then (`round` 2) each site's header, footer and home page links; logged-out visits to a network site's home page links are LiteSpeed hits once the fill ends.
