title: Load plugins only where needed: update caches and bookkeeping options from a few plugins make pages learn again
body:
## What happens

Load plugins only where needed forgets what the site's pages learned (and every checked address) when a few plugins refresh their update caches or bookkeeping options from wp-admin or WP-CLI. After each forget, uncached page renders load every plugin until a plain visitor render learns again, and Keep pages cached's fill plus the per-address checks start over, which costs server CPU on every site with these plugins.

Seen in the forget log (`seoprostack_plugin_front_forgets`) of eight sites on 1.3.174, over about a day each:

| Option written | Writer | Kind | Why it is missed today |
|---|---|---|---|
| a bare 32-hex name, value `array('timeout' => …, 'value' => …)` | EDD Software Licensing's updater: older copies cache `plugins_api` details under `md5('edd_plugin_' . $slug . '_' . $beta . '_version_info')` with no prefix (e.g. Link Whisper's `vendor/EDD_SL_Plugin_Updater.php` L480; FluentRoadmap's update details on one site) | `delete_option` / `update_option` from WP-CLI and wp-admin update checks | `RECORD_OPTIONS` has only the prefixed form `edd_sl_` |
| `external_updates-<slug>` (e.g. `external_updates-scalability-pro`) | YahnisElsts Plugin Update Checker's update state | `update_option` on a plain wp-admin view | not listed; the prefix rule only treats names ending in `.` or `_` as prefixes |
| `mwai_settings_backups` | AI Engine's settings backups | `update_option` on a plain wp-admin view | listed as the prefix `mwai_settings_backup_`, which the plural name does not match |
| `mainwp_child_request_ids_cleanup` | MainWP Child | `update_option` over AJAX | listed as the prefix `mainwp_child_request_id_`, which `ids` does not match |

On one site a read-only `wp plugin list` / `wp eval` pair at the moment an updater's cache expired was enough to forget everything learned (forget log entry `delete_option <md5> (cli)`, matched to the command's time).

## Fix

In `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`:

- `record_write()`: treat a bare 32-hex option name as a record when its value is EDD's update cache shape (exactly the keys `timeout` and `value`). The value comes from the hook (`add_option` passes the new value, `update_option` the old one) or, for `delete_option`, from the stored row, as `option_hash()` reads it.
- Register `add_option` and `update_option` with two arguments so `front_option_changed()` can pass the value on.
- `RECORD_OPTIONS`: add `external_updates-`, `mwai_settings_backups` and `mainwp_child_request_ids_`; treat names ending in `-` as prefixes too, and update the docblock.

Not in scope: Kadence Blocks 3.8+ copies its design-token palette into `kadence_blocks_colors` when its sync signature changes, and that is the most frequent forget in the same logs (WP-CLI, after updates). A palette can change what a page renders without Kadence Blocks, so it stays a change; why the signature changes several times a day is a separate question.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes.
- On a site with an EDD-updater plugin: note `seoprostack_plugin_front_forgets`, run `wp plugin list` after deleting the plugin's bare-MD5 cache row (or wait for it to expire), and check that no new forget entry names that option; `seoprostack_plugin_front` stays learned.
- Saving a real setting from wp-admin still forgets (unchanged path).

title: Deploy check: an event the site's cron ran meanwhile counts as a failed cron run
body:
## What

`scripts/deploy-sites.sh` reported a network deploy of 1.3.175 as failed on one site while the plugin updated and loaded fine everywhere:

```
site https://<site>/	status=active-network	purged=yes	cron=4/5	home=200 pinned	FAIL: cron seoprostack_keep_settings failed (exit 1: Error: Invalid cron event 'seoprostack_keep_settings' )
```

`run_site_cron()` (`scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` L635–674) lists the plugin's scheduled events first (`cron_list_code`), then runs each with `wp cron event run <hook>`. `seoprostack_keep_settings` is a single event scheduled after an update (`SEOProStack_Presets_Keep`, `includes/class-seoprostack-presets-keep.php` L112–113). On a host whose own cron job runs WP-Cron every minute, the event can run (and so leave the list) between the deploy's listing and its run. WP-CLI then exits 1 with `Invalid cron event`, and the check counts a failure that is not one: the callback did run, in the site's own cron.

Not the same race as #1362 (inside Keep pages cached).

## Fix

In `run_site_cron()`, when the run exits non-zero and its output is WP-CLI's `Invalid cron event '<hook>'` with no fatal error or database error in it, count the event as run by the site's cron: a note (`cron <hook> ran meanwhile`) in `CRON_WARN`, not `CRON_FAILURE`, and not in `CRON_HOOKS_RUN` (it did not run in the deploy's process). Every other non-zero exit stays a failure.

Deploy tooling only: no changelog entry (`STANDARDS.md` docs rule).

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh scripts/deploy-sites.sh` clean.
- Read-only: on the affected network, `wp cron event list --fields=hook,next_run_relative | grep seoprostack_keep_settings` shows the event gone or rescheduled, consistent with the site's cron having run it.
- Next fleet deploy: no `Invalid cron event` FAIL lines; any race shows as a note.

title: Speed: keep text still while web fonts load (metric-matched fallback fonts)
body:
## What

Kadence sites load their Google Fonts with `font-display: swap`: text first shows in the browser's own sans-serif or serif font, then reflows when the web font arrives. Where the two fonts differ in width and height, headings rewrap, rows move and fixed boxes (a cookie banner) change height: layout shifts.

On one Kadence site, PageSpeed's mobile run (7 November 2026) had CLS 0.19 (score 77) from this: the consent banner `section#spcc-banner` grew from 355 to 380 px when its text reflowed, and the hero headings moved. With the web fonts blocked, CLS was 0.

## Proposal

New Speed feature, on by default (safe on any site: it changes only how text looks for the moment before the web font arrives): **Keep text still while fonts load**.

For each web font the page declares (an `@font-face` in the page, in a stylesheet of this site with fonts in it, such as the Kadence theme's local Google Fonts file in `wp-content/fonts/`, or a `fonts.googleapis.com` link's `family=`), when its metrics are known:

- add a fallback face, `"<Family> Fallback"`, from a local system font sized to match: `src: local("Arial")` (and its metric twins Liberation Sans and Arimo) for sans-serif, display and handwriting fonts, `local("Times New Roman")` (Liberation Serif, Tinos) for serif ones, with `size-adjust` from the average character width and `ascent-override`, `descent-override` and `line-gap-override` from the font's metrics, for regular and bold separately; and a second one from Roboto or Noto Serif, for Android, which has no Arial;
- put it after the web font in the page's own `font-family` declarations (`<style>` blocks, including Kadence's `--global-*-font-family` custom properties and Kadence Blocks' per-block CSS);
- print the faces first in the head, with a line that starts loading them, so they are ready for the first paint.

The same approach as Next.js's `next/font` (`adjustFontFallback`) and Nuxt's fontaine. The metrics come from `@capsizecss/metrics` (MIT, by SEEK; Google Fonts and system fonts), stored in `assets/font-metrics/` with a refresh script like `scripts/update-brand-icons.*`. Monospace fonts and fonts with no known metrics are left as they are.

## Evidence (prototype)

The prototype rewrote each home page in a Playwright route, then measured layout shifts on a throttled phone (412x823 at 1.75x, 150 ms latency, 1.6 Mbit/s, CPU 4x):

| Site | Control CLS | With fallbacks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kadence site with a cookie banner | 0.190 (3/3 runs) | 0.021 (5/5 runs) |
| Kadence site whose fonts are in a linked `wp-content/fonts/` stylesheet | 0.266 | 0.003 (3/3 runs) |
| Kadence site A | 0.165 | 0 |
| Kadence site B | 0.062 | 0.005 |
| Kadence site C | 0.045 | 0.001 |
| Kadence site D | 0.021 | 0.051 |

Site D's bold 40 px heading wraps to three lines with the fallback (2 to 4% wider on that text): averaged metrics cannot match every string. Both sites rated poor (over 0.1) became good. The full fleet table, 3 runs per arm, goes in the PR.

## Files

- New: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-font-fallbacks.php` (pattern: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-jquery-footer.php`, page buffer at `template_redirect`), registered in `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php` and the plan in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-speed-plan.php` (`$defaults`).
- New: `assets/font-metrics/metrics.json`, `assets/font-metrics/LICENSE.txt`, `scripts/update-font-metrics.sh` and `.js` (pattern: `scripts/update-brand-icons.*`).
- Docs: `README.md` (feature section, On by default list, Credits, Unreleased), `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` clean.
- On a live Kadence site: the page has `<style id="seoprostack-font-fallbacks">` first in the head, and its fonts' declarations name the fallbacks; the throttled phone probe shows CLS at or below the prototype's.
- PageSpeed mobile on the site with CLS 0.19: CLS under 0.1.
- Screenshots after the fonts load are unchanged (the fallbacks are used only before).

title: Translations: block-title context entries use machine wording that differs from the reviewed plain entry (Add to shortlist, Like save and share)
body:
## What

Several `msgctxt "block title"` entries in `languages/seoprostack-*.po` are still marked `# machine translation` and use different words from the reviewed plain entry for the same English string. The block editor then names a block differently from the button visitors see.

Example (`languages/seoprostack-fr_FR.po` on `main`):

```
#: includes/features/class-seoprostack-post-reactions.php:375 ... blocks/shortlist-button/index.js:16
msgid "Add to shortlist"
msgstr "Ajouter à ma liste"

# machine translation
#: blocks/shortlist-button/block.json
msgctxt "block title"
msgid "Add to shortlist"
msgstr "Ajouter à la liste de présélection"
```

Found by comparing every context entry with the plain entry of the same `msgid` in the 1.3.169 catalogues (17 locales):

| Block title | Locales whose context entry differs from the plain entry |
|---|---|
| `Add to shortlist` | all 17 (e.g. de "Zur Merkliste hinzufügen" vs "Zur Merkliste", it "Aggiungi alla lista dei preferiti" vs "Aggiungi alla mia lista", nl "Toevoegen aan favorieten" vs "Op mijn lijst", pl "Dodaj do listy skróconej", ro "Adăugați la lista scurtă", lv "Pievienot īsajam sarakstam") |
| `Like, save and share` | de_DE/AT/CH, es_ES/MX (adds a full stop), et, lv, nl_NL/BE, pt_PT ("Curta, guarde e partilhe." is Brazilian), pt_BR (full stop) |
| `Your lists` | nl_NL/BE ("Uw lijsten" vs "Je lijsten": two registers) |
| `Client dashboard` | fr_CA ("Tableau de bord du client" vs "Tableau de bord client") |

Out of scope, verified correct: `Terms` (plain = taxonomy terms, "Begriffe"/"Termes" as in WordPress core) vs `msgctxt "licence terms link"` ("Bedingungen"/"Conditions"); `msgctxt "plugin"` `Active`/`Installed` in fr_CA (gender agreement).

## Why

The Property Services Directory sites use the plugin's "my list" word for the shortlist in every language (header label, panel title, add button, message button). The block titles should match, so editors and translators see one name. Low visitor impact: front-end buttons use the plain entry.

## How

- Files: `languages/seoprostack-*.po` (17 locales), then the compiled `.mo`, `.l10n.php` and `.json` files.
- For each `msgctxt "block title"` entry marked `# machine translation` whose `msgid` also has a plain entry: set its `msgstr` to the plain entry's reviewed `msgstr` (or a deliberate, reviewed variant) and remove the `# machine translation` flag. Keep one register per language (Dutch `je`).
- Compile: `bash scripts/translations.sh compile` (the repository's existing step; run before the release commit).
- If the catalogue generator (`scripts/translations.sh pot` or the machine-translation fill step) is what produced these entries, make it copy the plain entry's reviewed text into a same-`msgid` context entry instead of machine-translating it again, so the next refresh does not bring them back. The generator path for the fill step is not known from here; find it from `scripts/translations.sh`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `languages/seoprostack-de_AT.po`
- EDIT: `languages/seoprostack-de_CH.po`

- EDIT: `languages/seoprostack-es_ES.po`

- EDIT: `scripts/translations.sh`

Compiled `.mo`, `.l10n.php` and `.json` files change with them through `scripts/translations.sh compile`.

## Verification

title: LiteSpeed Cache preset: turn off LiteSpeed's CSS combine, UCSS and async CSS while Load the CSS each page uses first is on
body:
## What

**Load the CSS each page uses first** (Used CSS) steps aside on the whole site when LiteSpeed Cache combines CSS or makes its own unused or critical CSS (`SEOProStack_Used_Css::litespeed_css()`, `includes/features/class-seoprostack-used-css.php` L229–243: `optm-css_comb`, `optm-ucss`, `optm-css_async`). Nothing tells the site owner, and LiteSpeed's versions need QUIC.cloud.

Seen on one Kadence site (7 November 2026, point-in-time): Used CSS on, LiteSpeed Cache's **Load CSS Asynchronously** on. Used CSS stepped aside; QUIC.cloud's critical CSS was still queued ("QUIC.cloud CCSS in queue" in the cached page), so 20 of 21 crawled pages served every Kadence, Kadence Blocks, Fluent Forms and IndieWeb stylesheet as render-blocking. The home page alone was covered. Turning the LiteSpeed option off by hand fixed it.

## How

Follow the existing pattern in `presets/litespeed-cache.json` (LiteSpeed's Load JS Deferred is turned off while SEO Pro Stack's Delay scripts until people interact is on):

- `options`: `litespeed.conf.optm-css_comb`, `litespeed.conf.optm-ucss`, `litespeed.conf.optm-css_async` set to `""`.
- `defaults`: `""` for each (fresh LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.3 stores `''`).
- `when`: `["single_site", "feature:used_css"]` for each, so they change only where Used CSS is on.
- `settings`: labels from LiteSpeed's `src/lang.cls.php` (**CSS Combine**, **Generate UCSS**, **Load CSS Asynchronously**), a description saying they are turned off while Used CSS is on, and the usual values map.
- `notes`: one sentence on why.
- `docs/presets.md` → owner's decisions: one line.
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`: changelog line (same PR).

The preset's save goes through LiteSpeed Cache's own code (`SEOProStack_Litespeed::save_through_plugin()`), which purges, so cached pages built with LiteSpeed's CSS go.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`; `scripts/preflight-release.sh` passes the preset checks.
- Docker test site with LiteSpeed Cache: set `optm-css_async` to 1, turn Used CSS on, `wp seoprostack presets diff litespeed-cache` lists the three settings, `apply` sets them to `""`, `undo` restores 1; with Used CSS off, `diff` does not list them.

title: Redirect to the main address before WordPress loads (bare domain to www takes 1-5 s)
body:
## What

Visitors who open a site at its other address (the bare domain when the site is at `www.`, or the reverse) wait for WordPress to load in full before it sends them on: the 301 carries `x-redirect-by: WordPress` and `x-litespeed-cache: miss`, so no page cache answers it.

Measured on 7 November 2026 (curl, time to first byte of the 301, from London, Hostinger LiteSpeed behind Cloudflare), bare domain → `www.`:

| Site | First request | Next request |
|---|---|---|
| one Kadence site on a network | 4.37 s | 0.07 s (Cloudflare cached the 301) |
| another network site | 3.91 s | 0.11 s (`cf-cache-status: HIT`) |
| a single site | 5.00 s | |
| another network site | 1.04 s | |
| a single site | 0.64 s | |

Cloudflare keeps a 301 only for a while and per data centre, and sites without Cloudflare never get it cached. People who type the bare domain, or follow an old link to it, see a blank tab for seconds before the page cache can help. One network already has a hand-written `.htaccess` rule for its main domain only.

## Proposal

A new Speed feature, on by default (safe on any site: it only answers sooner with the redirect the site already makes), **Redirect to the main address before WordPress loads**:

- Candidates: each site's own host (single site: `home`; network: every site's domain), and its other address (with or without `www.`), leaving out any that is itself a site's address.
- Check each candidate from the server: `HEAD https://<other>/?seoprostack-host-check=<random>` without following redirects; keep it only when the answer is 301 or 308 to the site's own host. The query string is left out of the rules, so the check always reaches WordPress, never our own rule, and the random value keeps it out of Cloudflare's cache.
- Write a marked block at the top of the root `.htaccess` (as the background requests block in `SEOProStack_Plugin_Fixes` does), per checked host:

  ```
  RewriteCond %{HTTP_HOST} ^example\.com$ [NC]
  RewriteCond %{REQUEST_METHOD} ^(GET|HEAD)$
  RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} !^/\.well-known/

title: Image loading: pictures whose block names another attachment get no smaller sizes
body:
## What happens

Kadence Image blocks from an imported template can keep the template's attachment ID: the block's `"id"` and the picture's `wp-image-N` class name an attachment that does not exist on the site (or a different one), while `src` points at the right file in the site's uploads.

WordPress finds a picture's sizes through that ID (`wp_filter_content_tags()`), so it adds no `srcset`, `sizes`, `width` or `height`, and every visitor gets the full-size original.

Seen on one Kadence site (7 Nov 2026): all six pictures on the home page, and two other pages, say `wp-image-2864`; that ID does not exist. The right attachment (found by its address) has 683, 768 and 1024 px copies, with AVIF and WebP. Phones fetched the 1365×2048 original instead: 294 KB, 162 KB, 136 KB and 83 KB AVIF before the page's largest paint, 675 KB in all. PageSpeed mobile: 79, LCP 5.7 s. It is the only one of 13 Kadence sites checked with this, and the only one whose early pictures are full-size.

## Fix

In Image loading (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`), a `wp_content_img_tag` filter that runs before `content_image()` (so its size check sees the width and height):

- only for a tag with a `wp-image-N` class and no `srcset`, whose `src` is in this site's uploads and is not an SVG;
- left alone when attachment N owns the `src` file: core has already decided;
- otherwise find the attachment that owns the file (`attachment_url_to_postid()`, after removing a `-WxH` or `-scaled` size suffix), and call core's own `wp_img_tag_add_width_and_height_attr()` and `wp_img_tag_add_srcset_and_sizes_attr()` with it, as core would have with the right ID.

The page is not rewritten beyond what core adds to every other picture. The browser picks the smallest copy at least as large as the picture shows, so nothing is less sharp than now. One lookup per such picture, remembered for the request; cached pages skip it.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`: hook in `boot()`, new method.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`: Unreleased entries.

## Verification

- Test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`): a page with a Kadence Image block whose `id` and `wp-image-N` name a missing attachment, and one naming a different attachment. Both get `srcset`, `sizes`, width and height from the right attachment; a correct picture, an SVG and an external picture are unchanged; PHP log empty.
- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- After release, on the site: the home page's pictures carry `srcset`; PageSpeed mobile pictures before LCP fall well below 675 KB.

title: deploy-sites.sh: remove old run folders on the host after a deploy
body:
## What

`scripts/deploy-sites.sh --apply` should remove its own old run folders on the host after a successful deploy, keeping the newest few for rollback.

## Why (measured)

Each apply makes `~/.<slug>-deploy/<tag>-<stamp>/` on the host (`apply()`, `scripts/deploy-sites.sh` L395–424). It holds the zip, `deploy-remote.sh` and `backups/`, about 22 MB per install for SEO Pro Stack. Nothing removes them. On one shared hosting account (7 November 2026), about 330 run folders from v1.3.158 to v1.3.179 used **9.8 GB**. A one-site-at-a-time fleet run makes one folder per site per release, so the total grows by roughly 13 × 22 MB per release. Hosting plans count this against the account's disk quota.

## How

1. In `apply()`, after a successful install (status 0, after the "Deployed … To undo" line), prune on the host. Remove `$base/v*-*Z` run folders except:
   - the current run;
   - the folders of the newest `N` tags (default 3, so a rollback to the previous two releases stays possible);
   - any folder a running deploy holds (the lock from `lock_take` in `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`).
2. Option `--keep-releases N` (0 = keep everything, the current behaviour), and say in the output what was removed and how much space it freed.
3. Touch only folders that match the run-folder pattern (`v<version>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>`). Other files in `~/.<slug>-deploy/` (helper scripts, hand-made backups) stay.
4. `scripts/deploy-sites.sh` and `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` are core files (`scripts/core-files.txt`). Preflight already reports both differ from the starter. Make the change in the starter first, or in an `sps-own` block, as `STANDARDS.md` → Agent docs says.

## Files

- `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`: `apply()` L395–424, option parsing, usage text.
- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: lock helpers (`lock_take`), if the prune runs there.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` / `RELEASING.md`: where deploys are described, one line on retention.

## Verification

- `shellcheck scripts/deploy-sites.sh scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`.
- Against a test host or a throwaway folder with dummy run folders for 5 tags: after an apply, only the newest 3 tags' folders and the current run remain; other files untouched; `--keep-releases 0` removes nothing.
- One real deploy: the output lists the removed folders and the space freed.

title: WebP and AVIF images: restart the background conversion when what it makes changes without a settings save
body:
## What

**WebP and AVIF images** stops converting for good when the formats it makes change without a settings save. Its background batch (`seoprostack_nextgen_batch`) starts only when:

- the Next-gen settings are saved (`setting_saved()`);
- a picture is uploaded, edited or replaced (`metadata_updated()` / `metadata_committed()`);
- the Media Library bulk action runs (`handle_bulk()`);
- the rules sync for a site new to them (`sync_rules()`);
- someone opens the feature's settings panel (`panel_status()`).

When the queue is empty, `run_batch()` clears the hook. Later changes to what the queue makes, `signature()` (formats and qualities), mark every attachment as waiting but schedule nothing:

- the server's image editor gains AVIF (`can_make('avif')` turns true after a host upgrades ImageMagick);
- a new setting's default reaches the site (#404), for example **Make AVIF copies**, on by default.

The pictures then wait until someone happens to open Media settings, which on a network's sub-sites or a site run by presets can be never.

## Evidence (live, 1.3.179, 7 Nov 2026)

- On one 11-site network, 10 sites had `nextgen_images` and `nextgen_avif` on, `formats()` = avif+webp, and `waiting()` = 1–169 attachments each (326 in all), but no `seoprostack_nextgen_batch` event. Their `_seoprostack_nextgen_done` values were all `webp:90s`, and the one site with `avif:70s,webp:90s` had nothing waiting. Sub-site WP-Cron was running (events due within the minute).
- Effect: browsers got WebP rather than AVIF for every picture. Same picture: WebP 82 KB vs AVIF 57 KB (30% smaller). On a slider home page the LCP picture was the WebP.
- All 12 single sites checked had nothing waiting.
- Calling `SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images::schedule()` on each stalled site started the conversion.

## How

In `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`, `boot()` (after the `enabled()` return): on WP-Cron requests and admin screens, at most once a day per site, schedule a batch when pictures wait and none is scheduled:

- an autoloaded option holds the time of the last check, so the daily gate costs no extra query;
- `wp_next_scheduled(self::HOOK)` first (the cron array is already loaded); then `self::waiting(1)` (one indexed query); then `self::schedule()`.

Keep `run_batch()` unchanged. A disabled feature does nothing (the hook is added after the `enabled()` return).

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`: `boot()`, a new `maybe_restart()`, a new option constant.
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`: one line under Unreleased (`STANDARDS.md` docs rule).

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`): turn the feature on, let the queue finish, then set an attachment's `_seoprostack_nextgen_done` to an older signature and clear the hook (`wp cron event delete seoprostack_nextgen_batch`). Delete the daily option, run `wp cron event run --due-now`, and check that `wp cron event list` shows `seoprostack_nextgen_batch` again. A second run within the day does not query again.
- Live, after deploy: `waiting()` stays 0 on the fleet, and no site has waiting pictures without a scheduled batch.

title: Keep pages cached: refill every Page after LiteSpeed's Pages purge rule empties them on a post save
body:
## What happens

On a LiteSpeed site, saving or publishing any post or page empties **every WordPress Page** from the cache. Keep pages cached then reopens only the home page, the saved post and the posts page, so visitors (phones included) get uncached Pages until LiteSpeed Cache's crawler gets round to them, up to a day later.

Seen on one Kadence site on Hostinger (7 November 2026, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.180, LiteSpeed Cache with its default purge rules): at 20:14 UTC an automatic update with no user (revision author 0) saved the privacy policy page. At 20:28, 18 of the site's first 20 Pages answered a phone with `x-litespeed-cache: miss` (0.64–1.24 s). The privacy policy page was cached, and so was the only Post in the list (`post` type). The check page (`/?seoprostack-held=1`) stayed held, so no full fill started either.

## Why

- LiteSpeed Cache's **Purge Rules For Publish/Update** include **Pages** (`purge-post_p`), on by default. `\LiteSpeed\Purge::_get_purge_tags_by_post()` adds the `PGS` tag for any post of a built-in or viewable type, and `\LiteSpeed\Tag::_build_type_tags()` gives `PGS` to every `is_page()` view, the static front page among them. So one save purges every Page. **All pages** (`purge-post_all`) purges `*`.
- Neither goes through `_purge_all()`, so `litespeed_purged_all` (which starts our full fill) never fires. LiteSpeed fires `litespeed_purged_post` with the post ID after adding the tags (`_purge_post()`).
- `SEOProStack_Keep_Pages_Cached::post_changed()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php`) queues only `post_urls()`: the home page, the post and the posts page.
- The check page is the front page, so it is purged too. But the post fill's `hold()` opens it again (built, then a hit) and leaves `held` true, so `check()` never sees it go missing.

## Fix

- Hook `litespeed_purged_post`. When the page cache is LiteSpeed (`SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::page_cache()`), **Pages** or **All pages** is on (`SEOProStack_Litespeed::conf('purge-post_p' | 'purge-post_all', false)`), and LiteSpeed applied its rules to that post (type built-in or viewable, as `_get_purge_tags_by_post()` decides), call `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Queue::fill_later(false)`. That fills the site's main pages, then starts LiteSpeed's crawler (or opens the rest where it is off), as after Purge All. Purges one after another (a run of saves) still move the fill back, for up to 10 minutes after the first.
- Skip while `WP_IMPORTING`, as `visible_change()` does.
- Keep `post_changed()` so the saved post itself is reopened first.
- Docs: class docblock, README.md → Keep pages cached, changelog.txt, readme.txt.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Live, on a test site of the wpallstars network after deploy: save a page with `wp post update`, then confirm the queue is marked `full` with a batch scheduled. After the batch, confirm other Pages answer `hit` as a phone.

title: Image loading: the hero row after a short text-only Kadence row gets the opening row's preload
body:
## What

Image loading: when a page opens with a short Kadence Blocks row that shows only text on a colour or gradient (no picture), treat the row after it as the row the page opens with. Its background picture then gets what an opening row's gets: the preload at high priority from the head, at the size the screen needs (`SEOProStack_Kadence_Hero`, `SEOProStack_Kadence_Early`), and it counts as the first of the pictures that load straight away.

## Why (measured)

One Kadence site's home page (PageSpeed mobile, 7 November 2026, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.180): score 84, LCP 4.6 s simulated (observed 0.78 s). The LCP element is the second row's background slider slide (`li#splide02-slide01 > div.kb-bg-slide`). The first row is a heading band: a background slider with an empty slide under a gradient overlay, holding one column with two Advanced Headings.

`SEOProStack_Image_Loading::kadence_preload()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php` ~L213–267) only looks at `$blocks[0]`. That row has no picture, so nothing is preloaded, and the hero's picture is fetched at its full `-scaled.jpg` size (182 KB as AVIF on a 412 px phone) once the parser reaches it. Nothing counts it as a first picture either, so the next two content pictures (Property Hive listing photos far below, 195 KB and 36 KB) load straight away and compete with it.

Local Lighthouse (mobile, simulated, 3 runs each): as served, score 74–80, LCP 5.4–5.7 s, 604 KB of pictures in before the observed LCP. With the five listing pictures blocked: score 83–85, LCP 4.3–4.4 s, 215 KB. Of the other Kadence home pages checked (6), every one that opens with a picture row already gets the preload.

## How

1. `SEOProStack_Image_Loading`: a memoised helper that returns the row a post or page opens with, for its pictures: the first block, or, when that is a Kadence row with no picture of any kind (none on any background tab, device, overlay or slide, no video, no dynamic background), whose blocks are only columns, headings, paragraphs, lists and buttons, with no media file named anywhere and at most 300 characters of text, the block after it when that is a Kadence row.
2. `kadence_preload()`: use the helper for the row branch (the content must still open with a Kadence row). Leave the Advanced Slider branch as it is.
3. `SEOProStack_Kadence_Rows::first_row()` (`includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-rows.php` ~L379–394): the same row from the helper, so a row with a normal background picture is not made to wait as well.
4. Docblocks and docs: `README.md` (Image loading), `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt` `= Unreleased =` entries (`STANDARDS.md` docs rule).

Never less sharp: the same picture and sizes rule; only which row counts as the opening one changes, and only after a short text-only row.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`: `kadence_preload()`, new helper.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-rows.php`: `first_row()`.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`): a page opening with a heading-only Kadence row then a row with a background picture prints `seoprostack-hero` (or a head preload), and no `sps-rows` wait style for the second row; a page whose first row has a picture is unchanged; a first row with an image, a spacer or long text leaves the page as before. No PHP messages.
- After release: PageSpeed mobile on the page above; record score, LCP and pictures before LCP before and after.

title: Image loading: make the missing 1536 and 2048 copies of Kadence hero pictures
body:
## What

Kadence hero pictures often lack WordPress's 1536 and 2048 copies, so the sizing script (`SEOProStack_Kadence_Hero`, `SEOProStack_Kadence_Early`, `SEOProStack_Kadence_Slider`) can only jump from the 1024 copy to the full upload. Phones and desktops then fetch the full 2000–2560 px upload when about 1,500 px is enough.

## Evidence (7 November 2026, 1.3.182, Hostinger sites, read-only probes)

`wp_get_missing_image_subsizes()` across media libraries:

| Site | Images | Missing 1536x1536 | Missing 2048x2048 | Hero pictures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (Kadence home, heading band + background slider) | 198 | 35 | 14 | missing both |
| B | 156 | 42 | 13 | missing 1536 |
| C (network site, Advanced Slider) | 169 | 161 | 151 | every slide missing both |
| D (network site, Advanced Slider) | 375 | 334 | 326 | every slide missing both |
| E | 3000 | 2415 | 1 | has both |

`1536x1536` and `2048x2048` are registered on every site; the uploads predate them or were made while something removed them (the metadata has a `cmplz_banner_image` size but not these two). SEO Pro Stack never removes them.

What the hero script works out in Chromium (`need` = device pixels painted × 1.1; copies on offer):

| Site | Screen | Box | Need | Copies | Fetched |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 412×823 DPR 1.75 | 412×569 cover | 1460 | 300, 768, 1024, 2560 | 2560 upload (182 KB AVIF) |
| A | 1350×940 | 1350×569 | 1485 | same | 2560 upload |
| B | 412×823 DPR 1.75 | 412×400 | 1027 | 300, 600, 768, 1024, 2000 | 2000 upload |
| B | 1350×940 | 1350×400 | 1485 | same | 2000 upload |
| E | both | | 946 / 1485 | 300 … 1536, 2048 | 1536 copy |

PageSpeed mobile on A: 84, LCP 4.6 s simulated; 607 KB of images start before LCP, the hero 182 KB of them.

## Fix

When `SEOProStack_Hero_Picture::get()` reads a picture's metadata (every hero, slider and row picture path), and the attachment lacks uncropped core sizes WordPress would make for it (`medium`, `medium_large`, `large`, `1536x1536`, `2048x2048`, as `image_resize_dimensions()` decides), queue the attachment (one option, capped) and schedule a background batch. The batch makes only those sizes with `wp_update_image_subsizes()` (limited through the `wp_get_missing_image_subsizes` filter; from the scaled file when the original is gone), a few attachments per run within a time budget, records the attempt on the attachment so a failure is not retried for a week, and purges and re-warms only the page it was seen on (LiteSpeed `Po.<id>` tag, else `SEOProStack_Page_Cache::purge_posts()`; Keep pages cached queue). Next-gen images makes AVIF/WebP copies of the new files through its existing `wp_update_attachment_metadata` hook.

Adding copies never makes a browser pick a larger file than before (it takes the smallest copy that is enough), so never less sharp. Disk: two JPEG copies plus their AVIF/WebP per hero picture, only for pictures pages show in Kadence rows.

Files: `includes/class-seoprostack-hero-picture.php`, new `includes/class-seoprostack-picture-sizes.php`, `includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php` (`boot()` registers the batch hook), `uninstall.php` (option), `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

- Local test site: an upload with its 1536/2048 sizes removed from metadata and disk; open the page; the batch makes them; the hero script then lists 1536/2048 and a 412 px DPR 1.75 phone fetches the 1536 copy.
- Live after release: site A's hero script lists 1536/2048; PageSpeed mobile on site A before/after.
- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`; PHP log clean.

title: Image loading: new picture sizes are sent as JPEG until WebP and AVIF images' next batch
body:
## What

Image loading's missing picture sizes (#1406, 1.3.183) make a Kadence row or slide picture's 1536 and 2048 copies in a cron run, then purge and reopen the page it was seen on. WebP and AVIF images only schedules its batch for them (`SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images::metadata_updated()` → `schedule(5)`), so the new copies have no AVIF or WebP until the next cron pass.

## Evidence (one Kadence site, 1.3.183, 7 November 2026)

- 23:27:00Z: the run made `…-1536x1152.jpg` and `…-2048x1536.jpg` for the home page hero (2560×1920); the page's hero data now offers 300, 768, 1024, 1536, 2048, 2560, and phones (412 px, DPR 1.75, need 1,460) and desktops (1,350 px, need 1,485) choose the 1536 copy.
- 23:29Z: `…-1536x1152.jpg` with `Accept: image/avif,…` → `image/jpeg`, 278,691 bytes; the 2560 upload it replaces → `image/avif`, 185,835 bytes. The `.avif` and `.webp` of the 1536 and 2048 copies did not exist; `seoprostack_nextgen_batch` was due, 157 s overdue (the host's cron runs every few minutes).
- Responses are `cache-control: private`, `vary: Accept`, Cloudflare `BYPASS`, so with copies at the same address the gap lasts until the batch runs. With **Copies at their own addresses**, the hero data's `image-set()` is worked out when the page is rendered, and WebP and AVIF images does not purge pages after converting, so a page rendered in the gap could be cached without the new copies' AVIF for the cache's lifetime.

## Fix

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`: new public `convert_now($attachment_id)`, which takes the picture's claim (`SEOProStack_Media_Storage::lease(self::CLAIM . $id)`) and calls `convert_claimed()`, as `convert_part()` does; nothing when the feature is off or another batch holds the claim.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-picture-sizes.php`: `make()` calls it after `wp_update_image_subsizes()` adds sizes, before `run()` purges and reopens the page, so the page is cached with copies that already have their AVIF and WebP.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Test site with WebP and AVIF images on: a picture with 1536/2048 removed; after one visit and one `seoprostack_picture_sizes` run, `…-1536x…jpg.avif` and `.webp` exist and the attachment is marked converted (`_seoprostack_nextgen_done`), with no Next-gen batch run.
- Live, after deploy: the same site's next picture (or another site's hero) has its `.avif` within the same run; a phone fetches the 1536 copy as `image/avif`.

title: Load plugins only where needed: Bookly's booking form files hold up the first paint
body:
## What

On a Kadence site that uses Bookly, the home page scores 88 on PageSpeed mobile with first paint at 3.1 s. About 20 Bookly files sit in the head and hold up the first paint: `tailwind.css`, `bookly-main.css`, `intlTelInput.css`, `bookly.min.js` (67 KB), `intlTelInput.min.js`, `moment.min.js`, `hammer.min.js`, the Files add-on's `jquery.fileupload.js` and others. Lighthouse puts the render-blocking time at up to 1.4 s per file. The page's only Bookly shortcode is a `[bookly-form]` inside a Kadence modal, so nobody sees it before clicking.

"Load plugins only where needed" is right to keep Bookly on that page, because its content has the shortcode. What needs fixing is where Bookly prints its files.

## Why it is safe to move them

- Bookly's `Lib\Base\ShortCode::init()` enqueues the booking form's styles and scripts on `wp_enqueue_scripts` when the page's posts have the shortcode (`needToIncludeAsset()`, asset method `print`), or on every page (`enqueue`). Both go in the head.
- The form's markup is an empty container. Its start-up script (`frontend/modules/booking/templates/short_code.php`) calls `window.bookly(...)` only once `document.readyState` is `complete`, after every footer script has run.
- WordPress prints styles enqueued after the head (`print_late_styles()`) just before the footer scripts, so the CSS is in place before `bookly.min.js` fills the form.

## Change

A new `SEOProStack_Bookly_Assets` (`includes/class-seoprostack-bookly-assets.php`), booted by "Load plugins only where needed" on the site's pages. When every Bookly shortcode in the page's posts is `[bookly-form]` and the content has no Bookly blocks, it does two things:

- Moves Bookly's scripts to the footer (`group` 1). These are the handles starting `bookly-` or served from a `plugins/bookly*` folder, which covers the add-ons.
- Dequeues Bookly's styles in the head and enqueues them again on `wp_footer` before `print_late_styles()`.

Pages with other Bookly shortcodes (appointment lists, the customer cabinet) or Bookly blocks are left alone, because those print their markup on the server and need their CSS at first paint.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `includes/class-seoprostack-bookly-assets.php`
- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`
- EDIT: `README.md`
- EDIT: `readme.txt`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`

## Verify

- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`
- Live page, logged out:
  - No Bookly `<link>` or `<script>` in the head, and Bookly's files are printed at the end of the body.
  - The modal's booking form opens and loads its first step, with no console errors.
  - PageSpeed mobile shows no Bookly entry under render-blocking requests.

title: Bookly's stylesheets go back to the head with Kadence (WordPress core hoists late styles)
body:
## What happens

Since 1.3.185 (#1414), Load plugins only where needed moves Bookly's booking form scripts to the footer and takes its 7 stylesheets out of the head, enqueueing them again at `wp_footer` priority 1.

On a live Kadence site with a `[bookly-form]` shortcode, the scripts are now in the footer, but the 7 stylesheets are still in the head: they print just before `</head>`, after every other style, and still hold up the first paint.

## Cause

WordPress 6.9 and later, with a classic theme such as Kadence, runs `wp_hoist_late_printed_styles()` (`wp-includes/script-loader.php`, hooked from `wp_load_classic_theme_block_styles_on_demand()`). It captures the styles `print_late_styles()` would print in the footer and moves them to the end of the head through the template enhancement output buffer. Styles enqueued again in `wp_footer` are late styles, so they go back to the head.

The test-site check for #1414 used a block theme, where core does not hoist. With Kadence active on the same test site, the head has the same 7 Bookly stylesheets (reproduced).

## Fix

`includes/class-seoprostack-bookly-assets.php`: print Bookly's styles with `wp_styles()->do_items()` right after `wp_print_footer_scripts` (priority 21), not enqueue them again, and take any Bookly styles enqueued while the form renders off the queue just before it (priority 19), so core's capture never sees them. The page's load event waits for those stylesheets, and Bookly's start-up script waits for `readyState` "complete", so the form's CSS is still in place before the form is filled.

## Verification

- Test site with Kadence and Bookly 28.7: head Bookly tags 0, the form renders its steps, no console errors.
- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- After release: on the live Kadence site, head Bookly tags 0; the modal opens with the form styled.

title: Used CSS: load the full stylesheets once the page has loaded
body:
## What

**Load the CSS each page uses first** (Used CSS) puts each page's used rules in the page and loads the full stylesheets without blocking (`media="print"`, switched back on load). Those full stylesheets still start downloading as soon as the browser reads the head, so on a slow phone they share the connection with the pictures and fonts the first screen needs. Lighthouse's simulated LCP counts every request that starts before the observed LCP, so 20 to 30 full stylesheets cost several points on every Kadence site.

## Evidence

Local Lighthouse 12 (mobile, simulated throttling), each home page served through a local proxy so only the HTML changes; 3 or 4 alternating runs per variant (8 November 2026, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.187):

| Kadence site | Now (score, LCP) | Full stylesheets after the load event |
|---|---|---|
| Site A | 81–83, 4.6–4.9 s | 85–87, 3.8–4.1 s |
| Site B | 83–84, 4.6 s | 89–91, 3.4–3.7 s |
| Site C | 79–82, 5.0 s | 86–88, 3.8–3.9 s |
| Site D | 83–91, 3.1–4.2 s | 86–93, 2.7–3.7 s |

A layout check (`getComputedStyle` of every visible element and its box, with the full stylesheets held back, then again once they had loaded) found **0 differences** on 9 home-page and screen-size pairs across 6 Kadence sites (mobile 412 px and desktop 1,350 px), and with the mobile menu drawer open. The only difference found was where a script **Delay scripts** holds (Readabler) ran before the full stylesheets: its voice-navigation panel, hidden only by a rule in its stylesheet, showed at the bottom of the page. So held scripts must wait for the full stylesheets.

This is the step Debloat and FlyingPress 4 take (the full CSS later), which got one Kadence site to 100 on mobile in the conversation that led to #1194.

## How

- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-page.php`: with new setting `used_css_later` (child of `used_css`, troubleshooting group, on by default), each handled link keeps its place and `id` but its `href` moves to `data-seoprostack-href`; a small inline script before `</body>` gives each its address (as `media="print"`, switched to its media once loaded) on the `load` event or the visitor's first move, tap, scroll or key (capture listeners, so it hears them before other loaders). `window.seoprostackCss()` starts it and returns a promise kept when all have loaded or failed, or after 3 s. The `<noscript>` copy stays.
- Only where the page's content security policy allows inline scripts (`SEOProStack_Used_Css_Policy::allows($html, true)`), and not on pages with scripts another plugin holds until interaction (`litespeed/javascript`, `rocketlazyloadscript`, `pmdelayedscript`, `javascript/blocked`), whose scripts cannot be made to wait: those keep today's behaviour.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-delay-scripts.php`: the loader calls `window.seoprostackCss()` first, where present, and runs held scripts once it resolves.
- Changing the setting empties the page cache, like the feature's other settings.

## Verify

- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Test site with Kadence, Kadence Blocks and Fluent Forms: the page source has `data-seoprostack-href` links and `seoprostack-used-css-later`; after load every link has its `href` and its media; a held Delay scripts script runs only after the stylesheets have loaded; with the setting off, the page is as before.
- After deploy: local Lighthouse on the same home pages, and the layout check.

title: Speed: load Fluent Forms' scripts when a form comes near
body:
## What

New Speed feature, on by default: **Load Fluent Forms' scripts when a form comes near**. Fluent Forms prints its form scripts (`form-submission.js`, `fluentform-advanced.js`, and for some fields cropper, jQuery File Upload, lity, intl-tel-input, Choices, flatpickr) on every page with a form, usually below the first screen. On a phone they share the connection with the first screen's pictures and fonts, and Lighthouse's simulated LCP counts every request that starts before the observed LCP.

## Evidence

Local Lighthouse 12 (mobile, simulated throttling) on one Kadence home page with a Fluent Forms form below the first screen, served through a local proxy so only the HTML changed; 3 alternating runs each, with the full stylesheets already loading after the page (#1426) (8 November 2026, 1.3.187):

| Variant | Score | LCP |
|---|---|---|
| As is | 90–92 | 3.3–3.6 s |
| Fluent Forms' scripts never load | 93–94 | 3.0–3.2 s |
| ... and jQuery | 94–95 | 2.9–3.1 s |

Fluent Forms 6.2.17's `form-submission.js` starts with `"loading"===document.readyState ? addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", …) : setTimeout(s, 100)`, so it initialises when it loads late; `ff_reinit` re-initialises a form. On the #1426 test site (Kadence, Fluent Forms 6.2.17), `form-submission.js` held by **Delay scripts** until the first interaction still validated the demo form on submit (4 errors shown, no console errors).

## How (model: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-fluentforms-turnstile.php`, GH#1210)

- `script_loader_tag`: Fluent Forms' and Fluent Forms Pro's own scripts (address under `plugins/fluentform/` or `plugins/fluentformpro/`, and handles they depend on that are in those folders) become `type="seoprostack/near"` with `data-seoprostack-src`; their `-js-extra` / `-js-before` data scripts stay as they are.
- A small loader (like the Turnstile one) runs them in order (`async=false`) once a `.fluentform` form comes within 600 px of the screen (IntersectionObserver), a field gets focus, or the visitor taps a Kadence modal link; with no IntersectionObserver, straight away.
- Only Fluent Forms versions checked (6.2.17 and later, `FLUENTFORM_VERSION`), not on pages where a form is in the opening block (SEOProStack_Image_Loading's opening-block mark could tell), and not where a content security policy blocks inline scripts.
- Check Fluent Forms' conditional logic, multi-step forms, the phone field and file uploads on the test site, and that **Delay scripts** and Used CSS's words from scripts (SEOProStack_Used_Css_Scripts) still see these scripts (their classes must stay in the page's rules, as they run before the full stylesheets may have loaded).

## Verify

- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Test site with Kadence and Fluent Forms (and Pro): a form below the first screen submits, validates, shows conditional fields, the phone field's flags and file uploads after scrolling to it; a form in the first screen works straight away; a form in a Kadence modal works after opening it.
- Local Lighthouse on a Kadence page with a form below the first screen, 3 runs before and after.

title: Used CSS: WP Grid Builder's grid stylesheet and Google Fonts stop holding up the first paint
body:
## What

**Load the CSS each page uses first** (Used CSS) covers WP Grid Builder, one of the plugins SEO Pro Stack works with (`SEOProStack_Used_Css_Links::PLUGINS`), but two of its stylesheets still hold up the first paint, because neither is in a handled folder:

- `wpgb-grids-css`: the grid and card stylesheet WP Grid Builder writes to `wp-content/uploads/wpgb/grids/<name>.css` (`includes/frontend/class-assets.php` → `generate_stylesheet()`).
- `wpgb-fonts-css`: the Google Fonts its cards and facets use, from `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=…` (`get_fonts()`, `wpgb_get_facet_fonts_stylesheet()`), a request to another host on the first paint's path that also sends each visitor's address to Google.

A scan of 16 home pages on the owner's Kadence sites and up to 6 primary-menu pages each (about 100 pages) found no other render-blocking stylesheet outside the handled folders: only these two, on a listings page with a WP Grid Builder grid.

## Evidence

Local Lighthouse (mobile, simulated throttling, through a proxy that changes only the page's HTML), that listings page, alternating runs:

- base: 93, 93, 93 (FCP 2.05–2.23 s); second set 86, 94, 92.
- both stylesheets non-blocking: 99, 93, 100 (FCP 1.29–1.40 s in 2 of 3 runs).
- Google Fonts stylesheet only: 87, 93, 99. Grid stylesheet only: 93, 94, 92.

PageSpeed Insights (mobile) on that page: 93, FCP 2.0 s, LCP 3.0 s, LiteSpeed cache hit. Font Fallbacks already sizes "Montserrat Fallback" and "Montserrat Alternates Fallback" for it, so text does not move when the font arrives.

## How

title: Integrity checks: treat uploads .php files with no open tag, or starting with __halt_compiler(), as harmless
body:
## What

The daily integrity check (Uploaded PHP) reports two kinds of plugin data file that cannot run code. Treat them as harmless, as it already does for exit-guarded logs and empty `index.php` files.

1. **A `.php` file with no PHP open tag anywhere.** PHP runs only code inside `<?php`, `<?=` or `<?` tags (ASP and `<script language="php">` tags were removed in PHP 7), so such a file is plain text. Seen: `uploads/wp-mailster/wpmst.log.php` (WP Mailster log, 17 KB, no `<?`).
2. **A file whose first statement is `__halt_compiler();`.** PHP stops parsing there; the rest is data. Seen: `uploads/aios/firewall-rules/settings.php` (All In One Security firewall settings: `<?php __halt_compiler(); /** comment */ {json}`).

## Why

Fleet evidence (2026-11-08, Hostinger account, read-only): after real findings were cleaned up, these two plugin-written files were the only uploads PHP findings left that are certainly inert. Each email that lists harmless files teaches owners to ignore the email.

## How

File: `includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-folders.php`

- `harmless()` (line ~166): before the small-file checks, return `true` when `self::open_tag_after($file, 0)` finds no `<?` (reads in parts, up to `MAX_GUARDED_FILE`). Check `open_tag_after()`'s offset semantics first.
- `guard_end()` (line ~207): accept `T_HALT_COMPILER` as an alternative to `T_EXIT` after quiet tokens, followed only by `(`, `)` and then `;` or a close tag (whitespace or comments allowed). Once `__halt_compiler();` is complete, the file is harmless whatever follows: no close tag or `open_tag_after()` check needed, because nothing after it is parsed.
- Do not ignore other patterns seen in the same audit: `uploads/wph/environment.php` (ABSPATH guard, then code) and `uploads/smile_fonts/Defaults/charmap.php` (a large array) do run code when included, so they stay reported. The `seoprostack_integrity_ignore` filter covers them for site owners.
- Update README.md → File and account integrity checks, item 4, to list both cases.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-folders.php`
- EDIT: `README.md`

## Verification

- `composer` / project PHP lint and PHPStan checks that `DEVELOPMENT.md` lists.
- On a test site: put `uploads/t1.php` holding plain text with no `<?`, `uploads/t2.php` holding `<?php __halt_compiler(); {"a":1}`, and `uploads/t3.php` holding `<?php __halt_compiler() ?><?php echo 1;` (still harmless: PHP never parses past the halt). Also `uploads/t4.php` holding `text <?php echo 1;` must still be reported. Run the check (`wp cron event run seoprostack_integrity_checks`, the `HOOK` in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-integrity-checks.php`, repeated until the check finishes) and read `wp seoprostack health`.

title: perf: Media in cloud storage rebuilds its claim index on every update; uploads walk every inventory until it finishes (~1 min a picture at 100k)
body:
## What happens

After every SEO Pro Stack update, Media in cloud storage rebuilds its claim index from scratch, because the build state is keyed to `SEOPROSTACK_VERSION`, not to `CLAIMS_SCHEMA`. Until the rebuild finishes, `unique_filename_files()` cannot use the index (`claims_table(true)` returns `''`, so `stem_records()` returns `null`) and falls back to `stored_records()`: a full walk of every inventory, 100 attachment IDs a query, for **each** `wp_unique_filename()` call, which is to say for each uploaded picture.

The rebuild itself runs only 5 seconds per storage batch (`build_claims($start, 5)` in the batch runner), so on a large library it takes a long time to finish, and uploads stay slow for that whole time.

## Evidence (production multisite, 1.3.189, the day of the update)

- Library with attachment IDs up to ~104,000 (about 27,700 listings). Option `seoprostack_storage_job_claims` read `{"schema":"1","built":"","building":"1.3.189","cursor":76421}`, so the 1.3.189 rebuild was about a quarter done some time after the update.
- A WP-CLI import of 13 pictures to one post: `SHOW FULL PROCESSLIST` sampled every 2 s showed one connection (the importer's) running `SELECT DISTINCT post_id FROM wp_postmeta WHERE meta_key IN ('_seoprostack_storage', '_seoprostack_storage_removed') AND post_id < N ORDER BY post_id DESC LIMIT 100`, with `N` walking from ~104,000 down to ~4,800 and starting again from the top. About **one minute per picture**; the process sat at ~7% CPU with tens of thousands of voluntary context switches (round trips).
- Two installs on the same server whose rebuild had finished (`"built":"1.3.189"`) imported 41 pictures in a few seconds.

GH#981 added the index to fix exactly this cost (4.6 s per call at 17,000 pictures); the version key brings it back after each release, for as long as each rebuild takes.

## Code

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`:

- `claims_table()` (around line 617): `($complete && SEOPROSTACK_VERSION !== ($state['built'] ?? ''))` → `''`.
- `build_claims()` (around lines 719–729): starts a new build whenever `building` is not the running version, from `PHP_INT_MAX`.
- `unique_filename_files()` (around line 309): `null !== $records ? $records : self::stored_records()`.
- The URL index (`urls_table()` / `build_urls()`, around lines 773 and 947–957) and the kept originals' table (around lines 1048 and 1299–1313) use the same `SEOPROSTACK_VERSION` key, so their lookups also take the slow path after each update.

## Suggested fix (choose in review)

1. Key "built" on `CLAIMS_SCHEMA` (and a schema constant for the URL and originals tables), and bump the schema only when the hashing, the table layout, or the set of indexed files changes. A plain release then keeps the complete index.
2. If the version key exists to cover rows written by an older version that did not index (a downgrade then upgrade), record the lowest version that wrote since the last complete build and rebuild only when that version predates the index, or record the highest attachment ID covered by the last complete build and search only IDs above it during a rebuild, keeping index lookups for the rest.
3. Optionally, give `wp seoprostack media-storage` an action that finishes the builds in one run (time-bounded loop), for operators to run right after a fleet update.

## Verification

- On a library of 20,000+ pictures: update the plugin version, then upload 10 pictures via WP-CLI right away. Every `wp_unique_filename()` should read the claim table (`SELECT DISTINCT post_id FROM wp_seoprostack_storage_claims …`), not walk `wp_postmeta`; time per picture stays at the post-build level.
- Existing same-path tests: names claimed by other attachments, removed records and virtual `-scaled` siblings are still reserved.
- `scripts/lint.sh` and the PHP 7.4 lint pass.

title: Speed: WooCommerce Coming soon mode loads a 327 KB Inter font on every page where the theme already loads Inter
body:
## What

With WooCommerce's **Coming soon** mode on, even "store pages only", WooCommerce adds the fonts of its coming-soon page (Inter, weights 300–900, and Cardo) to the theme's theme.json fonts on **every** request, so WordPress prints their `@font-face` rules in `<style class="wp-fonts-local">` on every page:

```
@font-face{font-family:Inter;font-style:normal;font-weight:300 900;font-display:fallback;src:url('…/wp-content/plugins/woocommerce/assets/fonts/Inter-VariableFont_slnt,wght.woff2') format('woff2');…}
@font-face{font-family:Cardo;…src:url('…/wp-content/plugins/woocommerce/assets/fonts/cardo_normal_400.woff2')…}
```

Source: `Automattic\WooCommerce\Internal\ComingSoon\ComingSoonRequestHandler::init()` adds `experimental_filter_theme_json_theme()` on `wp_theme_json_data_theme` whenever `ComingSoonHelper::is_site_live()` is false (option `woocommerce_coming_soon` = `yes`), regardless of whether the current page shows the coming-soon screen (WooCommerce 11.2.1, `src/Internal/ComingSoon/ComingSoonRequestHandler.php` lines ~39–50 and ~186–275).

Where the theme also uses **Inter** (the Kadence theme's local Google Fonts, `wp-content/fonts/inter/…`), the browser takes WooCommerce's face for every weight and downloads its **327 KB** variable font (every character) before the first paint, while the theme's own preloaded Inter subset (49 KB) goes unused.

## Evidence

- One Kadence directory home page, Chromium 412×915: as served, font files Inter subset 48,556 + Sora 25,584 + **WooCommerce Inter 326,928 bytes**; the only Inter face loaded is `Inter 300 900` (WooCommerce's). With the `wp-fonts-local` block removed: the 327 KB file is gone and the theme's `Inter 400/500/600/700` faces are used.
- Same line breaks and layout; 3× zoom of the body text shows the same glyph shapes and widths (differences only in sub-pixel anti-aliasing).
- PageSpeed Insights mobile on four such home pages (8–9 Nov 2026): 80–88, LCP 3.9–5.4 s with FCP 1.6 s; the 327 KB font is a VeryHigh-priority request before LCP on each. Desktop 98–100.
- Fleet scan: 24 sites have `woocommerce_coming_soon=yes` with `woocommerce_store_pages_only=yes` and Kadence body font Inter; 3 more are in Coming soon mode with other body fonts (face declared, not downloaded).

## Fix

In **Lighter WooCommerce pages** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-woo-light.php`, on by default), only while `woocommerce_coming_soon` is `yes`: a page buffer (`template_redirect` `PHP_INT_MAX`, normal GET HTML views) removes each `@font-face` rule in `<style class="wp-fonts-local">` whose file is in WooCommerce's `assets/fonts/` folder **for a family the page also declares another way**: another `@font-face`, an on-site font stylesheet such as Kadence's `wp-content/fonts/`, or a Google Fonts link. Reuse `SEOProStack_Font_Fallbacks`' detection (make it a public `declared_families($html)`). A family only WooCommerce provides (Cardo, or Inter on a site that does not load it) keeps its rule, so no text falls back to another font; the page looks as it does once the store is live.

Not changed: WooCommerce's settings (Coming soon stays as the site owner set it), the admin and the block editor.

## Verification

- `php -l` and `scripts/lint.sh`.
- On a Kadence site with WooCommerce in Coming soon (store pages only) and Inter as the body font: the home page's `wp-fonts-local` block no longer names `Inter-VariableFont_slnt,wght.woff2`; Cardo's rule stays; the browser downloads no file from `woocommerce/assets/fonts/`; screenshot compare with the theme's Inter.
- A Coming-soon site whose fonts are not Inter: `wp-fonts-local` unchanged.
- PageSpeed Insights mobile before/after on one such home page.

title: LiteSpeed purge delivery: skip sites where LiteSpeed Cache is not running (stale subsite queue, endless admin-ajax 400s)
body:
## What happens

On a multisite network where LiteSpeed Cache is active on the main site only, `SEOProStack_Litespeed::deliver_purge()` runs at the end of every command-line run on the other sites too. A subsite can hold a purge in its own `litespeed.purge.queue` option (for example after `wp litespeed-purge blog <subsite id>` from the main site), but no LiteSpeed Cache runs on that subsite to take it. So every WP-CLI or host-cron run on that subsite opens its `admin-ajax.php` as `lscache_runner SEOProStack`, gets `400` (no action), and the queue never empties. With a host cron job running each site's WP-Cron every few minutes, this never stops.

## Evidence (9 November 2026, one Hostinger account, 24 networks)

- Cloudflare analytics, 45 minutes from the host's own address: 357 `GET /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php` with user agent `lscache_runner SEOProStack`, all `400`, all to subsites (the `-template`, `-onepage` and `-multipage` sites), about 8 per subsite. They pass through Cloudflare: the subsites have no LiteSpeed Cache Server IP and `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::resolver()` returns null when the page cache is not LiteSpeed.
- On every network, sites 2 to 4 had LiteSpeed Cache inactive and `litespeed.purge.queue` = `X-LiteSpeed-Purge: public,stale,<prefix>_` (80 stale queues). Main sites had `-1`.
- From about 02:59 UTC LiteSpeed's bot protection on the server answered `403 Access to this resource on the server is denied!` to the host's own address for every site on the account (static files too); it was still refused at 03:24 UTC. The admin-ajax `400` stream was the largest steady source of the host's own requests. (An operator workstation was refused at the same time for its own browser checks; that part is not this plugin's.)
- Setting those 80 queues to `-1` (LiteSpeed Cache's own "delivered" value) at 03:23 UTC stopped the stream. Backups of the previous values were kept.

## Expected

`deliver_purge()` (and the `http_request_args` / `http_api_debug` hooks) should do nothing on a site where LiteSpeed Cache is not running, for example when `LSCWP_V` is not defined or the `litespeed_conf` filter is absent. A waiting purge there cannot be delivered by opening that site's `admin-ajax.php`.

## Files

- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php`: `deliver_purge()` (from line 233) checks only `PHP_SAPI`, `is_server()` and `purge_waiting()`; `queued()` (line 321) reads the options directly, so a stale value on a site without LiteSpeed Cache counts as waiting.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php`: `resolver()` (line 279).

## Verification

On a network with LiteSpeed Cache active on the main site only: set a subsite's `litespeed.purge.queue` to a purge header value, run `wp cron event run --due-now --url=<subsite>`, and confirm no request to `<subsite>/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php` is made (for example with `http_api_debug` logging or the server's access log). On the main site, a waiting purge is still delivered as before.

title: watermark-images --dry-run fails when the mark's file is in cloud storage (real run works)
body:
## What

`wp seoprostack watermark-images --dry-run` (with or without `--stale`) fails with "The watermark picture’s file is missing." once Media in cloud storage has removed the mark's local file (site icon, logo or chosen picture), although the real run works: it restores the file first.

## Why

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`, `cli()` (around line 3001 in 1.3.191): `$mark = self::mark(!$dry);`. `mark($restore)` calls `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::ensure_local($id)` only when `$restore` is true, then checks `is_file(get_attached_file($id))`. A dry run therefore cannot read a drained mark, and `--stale` needs the mark's file to compute `mark_signature()`.

Seen on a multisite network with Media in cloud storage after a new site icon was set and drained: the dry run counted the stale pictures before the drain and errors after it; nothing else changed.

## Suggested fix

Either let the dry run read the mark without changing the site (fetch it to a temporary file that is deleted afterwards, and compute the signature from that), or, if that is unwanted, end the dry run with a clear message: the mark is in cloud storage, so the dry run cannot compare; the real run fetches it first.

## Verification

- Set a site icon, let the cloud drain remove its local file, then run `wp seoprostack watermark-images --stale --dry-run`: it lists the candidates (or prints the clear message) instead of "file is missing".
- The local file state after the dry run is the same as before it.

title: Core files differ from the starter
body:
## What

Compared with the starter at [wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding@e84ca77](https://github.com/wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/commit/e84ca772c5e9328d16cdf75ff8f96e5dbab1baa9): 7 of 85 core files differ from the starter. Run scripts/sync-core.sh, or change the starter first. Core files are the same in every plugin made from the starter, apart from the names (STANDARDS.md → Structure).

- `scripts/check-deploy-log.sh` (missing)
- `scripts/core-files.txt` (differs, behind)
- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` (differs, behind)
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh` (differs, behind)
- `scripts/sync-core.sh` (differs, behind)
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` (differs, behind)
- `RELEASING.md` (differs, behind)


## How

1. Next to this repository: `git clone https://github.com/wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding.git` (or `git -C ../wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding pull`).
2. Here, on a branch: `scripts/sync-core.sh --from ../wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding`, then review `git diff`.
3. Each file's class says what a sync does with it (DEVELOPMENT.md → Starter sync): **behind** and **missing** files are updated or added. A file **changed here** holds a change this plugin made that no starter version has: it goes into the starter first (a pull request, or an issue there with this plugin's case); sync after it is merged there, with `--discard-local`. Never keep a plugin-only change in a core file: move it to this plugin's own files or its own blocks. A **newer** file has a starter version the starter's default branch does not contain: sync from a starter ref that does. While a file is changed here or newer, a sync writes nothing.
4. Read the starter's `changelog.txt` since this plugin last synced, for changes that need work in this plugin's own files (its Setup class, `phpstan-plugin.neon`, `.distignore` entries, README or readme.txt sections).
5. `scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` pass; add a changelog line; open a pull request.

The daily Starter sync workflow (`.github/workflows/starter-sync.yml`) updates this issue while files differ and closes it once they match.

## Verification

`scripts/sync-core.sh --check --from ../wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding` reports that all core files match the starter.

title: fix: translated count strings keep the number first (~730 plural entries, 17 locales)
body:
## What

About 730 plural entries in SEO Pro Stack's bundled `.po` catalogues move the count behind the noun, which changes the meaning. The English starts with the count (`"%d table converted."`, `"%s short link updated."`); the machine translation reads as "table number N" or "plugin N":

- fr_FR `"%d table converted."` → `"Table %d convertie."` (= "table no. N converted")
- pl_PL `"%d tables converted."` → `"Konwertowane tabele %d."`
- ro_RO `"%d plugin"` → `"pluginul %d"`; `"%s short link updated."` → `"Legătura scurtă %s a fost actualizată."`

The same class was fixed in SEO Pro Directory (wpallstars/seoprodirectory#480, PR #481). Counts on main at `72293147`:

| Locale | Entries |
|---|---|
| pl_PL | 63 |
| ro_RO, fr_FR, fr_BE | 62 each |
| es_ES, es_MX | 61 each |
| pt_PT, pt_BR | 58 each |
| it_IT | 52 |
| fr_CA | 46 |
| de_DE, de_AT, de_CH | 26 each |
| nl_NL, nl_BE | 21 each |
| lv | 20 |
| et | 9 |

Some flagged entries are already correct (verb-first forms such as Latvian "Atrasta %d", or languages where count-after-noun is natural in a label). Check each one; don't rewrite blindly. Mostly admin-screen notices and counters.

## How

- Pattern: wpallstars/seoprodirectory PR #481. Hand-written corrections per locale that put the number first, as in the English (for example fr `"%d table convertie."` / `"%d tables converties."`, pl `"Przekonwertowano %d tabelę."` / `"… %d tabele."` / `"… %d tabel."`, with the right plural form per index). Keep the layout with `msgcat`, and remove the "machine translation" translator comment from entries you correct by hand.
- Keep every placeholder and its type (`%d`, `%s`, `%1$s`) and the number of `msgstr[n]` forms each locale's `Plural-Forms` needs.
- Compile with `bash scripts/translations.sh compile`; never hand-edit `.mo` or `.json`.
- Out of scope: entries whose English does not start with the count, and the `.pot`.

### Files Scope

- `languages/seoprostack-pl_PL.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-ro_RO.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-fr_FR.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-fr_BE.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-fr_CA.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-es_ES.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-es_MX.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-pt_PT.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-pt_BR.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-it_IT.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-de_DE.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-de_AT.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-de_CH.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-nl_NL.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-nl_BE.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-lv.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-et.po`
- `languages/*.mo` (compiled by `scripts/translations.sh compile`)
- `languages/*.json` (compiled by `scripts/translations.sh compile`)
- `changelog.txt`

## Verification

- Scan: with polib, list plural entries whose `msgid` starts with `%d` or `%s` and whose `msgstr[n]` does not start with the placeholder (allowing a leading verb). Only entries checked and judged correct should remain; list them in the PR.
- `msgfmt --check -o /dev/null languages/seoprostack-<locale>.po` passes for every changed locale.
- `bash scripts/translations.sh compile`, then `git status` shows only `languages/` and `changelog.txt` changes.
- `scripts/lint.sh` passes. A changelog entry under `= Unreleased =` in `changelog.txt`.
