title: Cloudflare: clear its copies of pages whenever LiteSpeed Cache or WP-Optimize clears them; Hosting needs warns on any-cookie cache rules
body:
## What

Add a Cloudflare purge connector. Whenever LiteSpeed Cache or WP-Optimize clears pages, SEO Pro Stack also clears Cloudflare's copies of those pages. Then sites can let Cloudflare cache HTML for logged-out visitors, and an edit or update shows up straight away instead of after the edge TTL.

SEO Pro Stack does not cache pages itself (the owner's rule in #1301 still holds). It only clears pages that another tool caches.

## Why

- **Origin protection.** On Hostinger's LiteSpeed servers, bot protection counts the requests that reach the server, per address, across every site on the account. On 9 Nov 2026, clicking through five pages of one fleet site quickly sent 32 requests to the server and the address was blocked (403) on every site. An edge HIT never reaches the server, so cached HTML takes the page request out of every click. (The beacon requests are handled in wpallstars/seoproanalytics#80.)
- **Today's gap.** LiteSpeed Cache's own Cloudflare option only covers Purge All (`src/purge.cls.php` `_purge_all()` → `CDN\Cloudflare::purge_all()`, verified in 7.9.3). Purging one post, the front page, a tag or a type never reaches Cloudflare. WP-Optimize has no Cloudflare purge. #1301 left purging single pages out of scope for this reason.

## Cloudflare facts this depends on (Cloudflare docs)

- On the Free plan you can purge by URL, hostname, tag or prefix, or purge everything. The limit is **5 purge requests per minute** (bucket of 25) and 100 operations per request. So purges must be queued and combined.
- On Free, cache rules can cache HTML ("Eligible for cache"), with an Edge TTL of at least 2 hours, and up to 10 rules.
- If the origin sends no `Cache-Control`, Cloudflare gives browsers the zone's Browser Cache TTL. Purging the edge cannot clear copies in visitors' browsers.

## Change

1. **Connection.** Setting: a Cloudflare API token limited to Zone → Cache Purge, and the zone ID. If LiteSpeed Cache's Cloudflare API is already connected, offer to reuse its key and zone. The token can also be set as a `wp-config.php` constant. Never print or log it. On multisite, each site sets its own zone.
2. **Tag HTML responses.** On front-end HTML for logged-out visitors, send `Cache-Tag`: a site tag (for example `sps-<blog>-html`) and, on singular views, `sps-<blog>-post-<ID>`. Check that LiteSpeed Cache keeps the header in its cached copy (curl the origin twice; the second answer should be `x-litespeed-cache: hit` and still carry it). If it does not, fall back to purging by URL.
3. **Listen to purges.** Use the hooks `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php:162-165` already uses:
   - `litespeed_purged_all` and `litespeed_purged_all_lscache`: purge the site tag.
   - `litespeed_purged_post` ($post_id), `litespeed_purged_front`, `litespeed_purged_frontpage`, `litespeed_purged_pages`, `litespeed_purged_posttype`, `litespeed_purged_tag`: purge the post tag plus the front and posts pages. Where LiteSpeed empties every page (its Purge Rules For Publish/Update set to Pages, the default; see the docblock at `class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php:349-358`), purge the site tag.
   - `wpo_cache_flush` (WP-Optimize, everything). Check the installed WP-Optimize for its single-page purge action before relying on it.
   - Leave out purges that do not touch HTML (`litespeed_purged_all_ucss`, `_cssjs`, `_object`, `_opcache` and so on).
4. **Queue and combine.** Collect purge targets during the request and send them once, after LiteSpeed's own purge (at `shutdown` or a short scheduled job, the way `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Queue::fill_later` works). Then the edge does not fetch the old copy back from the origin. A site-wide purge replaces any queued single purges. Stay within 5 requests per minute; on a 429, retry with backoff. Keep the last 20 results (time, scope, Cloudflare's answer) for Hosting needs.
5. **Refill after a purge.** After the Cloudflare purge, Keep pages cached should refill the origin as it does now, unchanged.
6. **Hosting needs.** Use `cf-cache-status` from `cdn_probe()` (#1301). If Cloudflare caches HTML and the connector is off, warn and give the setup steps. If the HTML answer gets a long browser `max-age` from Cloudflare (the zone's Browser Cache TTL, for example one year), warn: browsers will keep old pages that no purge can clear. The cache rule must set a short Browser TTL, or the origin must send `Cache-Control: max-age=0` for logged-out HTML.
7. **Docs.** Add the Cloudflare setup to README.md: the cache rule that caches HTML except for logged-in, cart and comment-author cookies, `/wp-admin`, `/wp-login.php`, `/wp-json`, `?s=`, previews and POSTs; a short Browser TTL; and Tiered Cache with Smart Topology (free). Say whether cookie matching works on Free; that was not confirmed from the docs, so check it in the expression builder and write down the result.

Ideas taken from Super Page Cache (wp-cloudflare-page-cache), not its code:
- a purge queue that does not overload the server;
- also purging related pages (home, archives);
- a header that shows whether a page was cached at the edge;
- a log of purges.

Not included: having SEO Pro Stack create the cache rule (that needs a broader Zone Rulesets Edit token); changing the cache key by device; APO.

## Found on a fleet site (Kadence, WooCommerce, LiteSpeed host, Cloudflare Free), 9 Nov 2026 (applied by hand there; use as the reference)

- **"Any cookie" rule.** The zone already had a cache rule that cached anonymous pages, but only with `http.cookie eq ""`. Cookie consent and analytics set first-party cookies on the first page, so every later click went past Cloudflare to the server: `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC` with any cookie, `HIT` with none. That is why quick browsing still tripped Hostinger's bot protection. This is likely common.
  - **Hosting needs check:** fetch the home page twice with no cookie and twice with a harmless made-up cookie (for example `sps_probe=1`). If the cookie-free fetch is `HIT` and the cookie fetches are `DYNAMIC`, warn: the edge cache skips every visitor with any cookie. Give the cookie list below.
- **Cookie list.** Skip Cloudflare's cache only on cookies that change what LiteSpeed Cache serves. LiteSpeed already serves one copy whatever the consent and analytics cookies are, so the edge can too. The list used on that site (cookie matching works on the Free plan; this rule is live there):
  - `wordpress_logged_in_`, `wp-postpass_`, `comment_author_`, `_lscache_vary`
  - `woocommerce_items_in_cart`, `woocommerce_cart_hash`, `wp_woocommerce_session_`
  - `seoprostack_maintenance_bypass`, `seoprostack_view_as`, `wp-health-check-disable-plugins`

  The rule also keeps `http.request.uri.query eq ""`, `not starts_with(path, "/wp-")`, `extension ne "php"`, Edge TTL `respect_origin` (2 h by default for a 200 with no headers) and Browser TTL `bypass_by_default`. Checked: basket, checkout, my-account and 404 answer `BYPASS`, because WordPress and WooCommerce send `no-cache`/`private`; Cloudflare does not cache 403s, so LiteSpeed's deny and challenge pages are never kept.
- **Mobile copy.** If LiteSpeed Cache's Cache Mobile is on and Cloudflare keeps one copy per URL, phones get whichever copy was fetched first. Hosting needs should point this out. On that site the owner chose one copy for all, so Cache Mobile was turned off.
- **Purge Everything works.** With LiteSpeed's Cloudflare API connected (a token limited to Zone Read and Cache Purge for one zone) and Clear Cloudflare cache on, `wp litespeed-purge all` cleared Cloudflare: the home page went from `HIT` (age 123) to `MISS`. Single-page purges are still the gap this issue fills.

## Files

- New `includes/class-seoprostack-cloudflare-purge.php` (connection, queue, API call, log).
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php`: reference pattern for the hooks and queue; refill order.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php`: `cloudflare_connected()` (line ~468), for reusing LiteSpeed's key.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`: `cdn_probe()` and the checks.
- `presets/litespeed-cache.json`: notes only. LiteSpeed's `cdn-cloudflare_clear` stays as it is.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `uninstall.php` (remove the settings).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Test on a LiteSpeed site behind a Cloudflare cache rule that caches HTML, with the token set:
  - Edit a page. Within a minute that page and the home page answer `cf-cache-status: MISS`, then `HIT`. Other pages stay `HIT`.
  - Purge All in LiteSpeed Cache: every HTML page answers `MISS`, and static files stay `HIT`.
  - Update a plugin: the same as Purge All.
  - Save 10 posts in a minute: at most 5 purge requests reach Cloudflare, and no 429 is lost.
- Same tests with WP-Optimize instead of LiteSpeed Cache.
- With no token set: no requests to Cloudflare, and no PHP warnings.
- The token never appears in HTML, the log, the debug log or Hosting needs.
- Hosting needs, on a zone whose cache rule uses `http.cookie eq ""`: the any-cookie warning shows. With the narrowed cookie list: no warning, and a made-up cookie gets `HIT` on the second fetch.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `includes/class-seoprostack-cloudflare-purge.php`
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php`
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`
- `presets/litespeed-cache.json`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`
- `uninstall.php`

title: t27: Website Setup board: task to clear Cloudflare's cache with LiteSpeed Cache
body:
## What

Add a **Website Setup** board task to SEO Pro Stack's Fluent Boards starter data that tells a site's owner, or their AI assistant, how to connect LiteSpeed Cache to Cloudflare. Then every **Purge All** (including the one after plugin and theme updates, and the deploy's WP-CLI purge) also empties Cloudflare's copy of the pages.

Target repository: wpallstars/seoprostack

## Why

On Hostinger sites behind Cloudflare with a Cache Rule that caches HTML, a LiteSpeed purge left Cloudflare serving old pages. A deploy on 9 November 2026 saw pages up to 6,353 s old on eight fleet sites after LiteSpeed reported `purged=1/1`. SEO Pro Stack's **Hosting needs** already warns about this (**Cloudflare keeps pages**, #1301), and the `litespeed_cloudflare` preset turns on **Clear Cloudflare cache** once a key and zone are set. The setup board has no task that gets the owner to that state. The owner wants this as a board task so client agents can do it once sites are handed over for self-hosting.

On 9 November 2026 this was set up on the operator's own sites with zone-scoped tokens, and it was verified. `wp litespeed-purge all`, and on a network `wp litespeed-purge blog <id> --url=<site>`, printed "Notified Cloudflare to purge all successfully". The home page's `cf-cache-status` went from `HIT` (age 3318) to `MISS`.

## How

### Files Scope

- starters/fluent-boards.json
- README.md
- readme.txt
- changelog.txt

### Details

Related: #1461 (SEO Pro Stack's own Cloudflare purge connector) can reuse LiteSpeed Cache's key and zone, so the token this task creates serves both.

Files:

- `starters/fluent-boards.json`: add one `fluentboards_tasks` item to the "Website Setup" board, directly after "Setup Cloudflare (domain DNS and security)". Array order sets `prev` (`chain_tasks()` in `includes/class-seoprostack-starters.php:275`). On boards that already exist, `wp seoprostack starters add fluent-boards` adds it after that task, matched by title. Bump `updated`.
- README "The setup tasks" section: regenerate with `scripts/readme-setup-tasks.js`, never by hand. The renumbered headings follow from that. Also update the "New: Fluent Boards starter data" or the setup-board paragraph if it lists the tasks.
- `changelog.txt` / `readme.txt` changelog, in the repo's usual style.
- Read `docs/presets.md` first (AGENTS.md → Task docs: starter data).

Suggested task (check the labels against LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.x's own screen strings before using them; keep the plain style of the other tasks):

- Title: `Clear Cloudflare's cache with LiteSpeed Cache`
- Description (Markdown):

  > LiteSpeed Cache keeps fast copies of pages on the server, and Cloudflare can keep its own. When LiteSpeed Cache empties its copies (Purge All, after updates), Cloudflare's stay until they expire, so visitors can see old pages. With a Cloudflare token, every Purge All empties Cloudflare too.
  >
  > 1. In Cloudflare, open **My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token → Create Custom Token**. Name it after the site. Permissions: **Zone → Cache Purge → Purge** and **Zone → Zone → Read** (LiteSpeed Cache looks the zone up with it). Zone Resources: **Include → Specific zone →** this site's domain. Create it and copy the token: Cloudflare shows it only once.
  > 2. In WordPress, open **LiteSpeed Cache → CDN → Cloudflare**. Turn **Cloudflare API** on, paste the token as the API token, leave the email empty, enter the domain, turn **Clear Cloudflare cache** on and save.
  > 3. Test with **Purge All** (LiteSpeed Cache in the admin bar or Toolbox): it says Cloudflare was notified.
  >
  > **Clear Cloudflare cache** empties the whole domain on Cloudflare. If other websites share this domain (on subdomains), leave it off and purge each address on its own. Never paste the token into a task or comment.

Test with `wp litespeed-purge all`. On a multisite network, use `wp litespeed-purge blog <id> --url=<site address>` instead: `all` empties every site's cache on the network, and without `--url` the main site's Cloudflare settings are used.
  >
  > Done when Purge All reports Cloudflare notified and the home page's `cf-cache-status` header is `MISS` straight after.

- Tasks never hold a key (README: "Tasks never hold a password or key").
- LiteSpeed Cache routes credentials by format (`src/cdn/cloudflare.cls.php`, `cloudflare_call()`): a `cfk_` key or 37–45 lowercase hex is a Global API Key (needs the email); anything else, including today's 53-character tokens, is sent as a Bearer token. So the email stays empty for a token.
- On a network, the Cloudflare options are per-site (`Base::$single_site_options`), so each subsite with its own domain gets its own token and zone.
- Without **Zone Read**, a Cache Purge–only token makes `try_refresh_zone()` (run on every LiteSpeed settings save) find no zone and clear the saved one. Keep both permissions in the task. The README's `litespeed_cloudflare` preset line (#1301) says "a Cloudflare API token limited to Zone → Cache Purge is enough": correct that too.

- `wp seoprostack starters diff fluent-boards` on a site with an existing Website Setup board lists only the new task as missing. `starters add` places it after "Setup Cloudflare (domain DNS and security)", and adding again adds nothing.
- README "The setup tasks" matches `starters/fluent-boards.json` (generated by `scripts/readme-setup-tasks.js`).
- The repo's own checks pass (see DEVELOPMENT.md).

## Out of scope

- Applying it to existing boards. The fleet's existing Website Setup boards are on networks that share one Cloudflare zone today, so their owner adds the task at handover, once each site has its own domain.

title: Remove CPT base: a renamed item's old short address gives 404 instead of redirecting
body:
## What happens

With **Remove CPT base** on, a renamed item of a chosen post type keeps its old name in `_wp_old_slug`, but its old short address (`/{old}/`) gives **404**:

- The request matches WordPress's `name` rule with no post type.
- `SEOProStack_Remove_Cpt_Base::resolve()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-remove-cpt-base.php`, ~line 249) looks for an item named `{old}` with `get_page_by_path()`, finds none, and returns the query vars unchanged.
- Core's `wp_old_slug_redirect()` then guesses post type `post` (no `post_type` query var), so it never finds the item's old slug.

The old address with the base (`/{base}/{old}/`) still redirects, as the rewrite rule names the post type. WordPress's 404 guess (`redirect_guess_404_permalink()`) only helps when the old name is a prefix of the new one.

Seen with SEO Pro Directory listings (post type `business`). SEO Pro Directory 0.4.136 handles its own types (seoprodirectory GH#494), but any other chosen type (products, courses, etc.) still 404s after a rename.

## Fix

In `resolve()`, when `get_page_by_path($path, OBJECT, $types)` finds no item and `$path` has no slash, look up a published item of `$types` whose `_wp_old_slug` is `$path` (one `get_posts()` with a `meta_query`, `fields => ids`, `posts_per_page => 1`). If found, return query vars with `post_type` set to its type and `name` set to `$path`. WordPress then 404s with the post type known, and `wp_old_slug_redirect()` sends a 301 to the new address. Alternatively, redirect to `get_permalink()` directly at `template_redirect` on a 404.

## Verify

- A site with Remove CPT base on for a type: rename an item (`wp post update <id> --post_name=new`). `curl -sI /{old}/` gives 301 to `/new/`; `/{base}/{old}/` still 301; an unknown name stays 404.
- The project's lint (phpcs/phpstan) passes.

title: Fixes for other plugins: serve Tutor LMS Pro's push service worker as a static file (each check now runs WordPress); unregister it when Notifications is off
body:
## What

Fixes for other plugins: serve Tutor LMS Pro's push-notification service worker (`/tutor-push-notification.js`) as a static file, so browsers checking it no longer run WordPress. Where the Notifications add-on is off but browsers still have the worker, serve a static file that unregisters it.

## Why

Observed on a fleet site on Hostinger shared hosting (LiteSpeed, Cloudflare) on 9 Nov 2026:

- Tutor Pro 4.2.0 `addons/tutor-notifications/classes/Push_Notification.php`: `__construct()` hooks `load_service_worker()` on `init`. On a request whose path ends in `tutor-push-notification.js`, it `readfile()`s the static `assets/js/tutor-push-notification.js` (2,148 bytes) and exits.
  - So every fetch boots WordPress, plugins and `init` (about 0.5 s of PHP) to return a fixed file.
  - The response has no cache headers, and LiteSpeed Cache does not cache it.
- `assets/js/register.js` registers the worker on every page: `navigator.serviceWorker.register(home_url + "/tutor-push-notification.js")`. Browsers re-check the worker script on navigations; service worker script checks bypass the HTTP cache by default.
  - Five quick page views produced 6 PHP fetches of the worker script, out of 32 origin requests in total.
- Hostinger's automatic CloudLinux/LiteSpeed CPU protection challenges visitors while the account is at its CPU limit. Uncached PHP requests like these feed that limit.
- Turning the add-on off is not enough. Browsers that registered the worker keep requesting the URL, and each request becomes a WordPress 404, still a full PHP run. On that site, a hand-written static file that unregisters the worker fixed it.

## Change

In `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`, next to the existing Tutor LMS Pro fix (#604 and #607, the `dbDelta()` enum fix), add a fix:

1. **Add-on on.** Tutor Pro is active and `tutor_addons_config['tutor-pro/addons/tutor-notifications/tutor-notifications.php']['is_enable']` is truthy.
   - Write a byte-identical copy of Tutor's `assets/js/tutor-push-notification.js` to `ABSPATH . 'tutor-push-notification.js'`, so the web server serves it without PHP.
   - Refresh it when Tutor Pro's version changes (the `upgrader_process_complete` hook, or a version stamp checked on `admin_init`).
2. **Add-on off, previously on.** Keep a small static file that unregisters the worker:
   - `install`: `skipWaiting()`
   - `activate`: `registration.unregister()`

   Without it, the browsers that registered the worker keep asking WordPress for it.
3. **Leave other files alone.** Mark the files SEO Pro Stack writes with a first-line comment. Never overwrite or delete a file at that path without the marker.
4. **Remove on deactivate and uninstall** (`uninstall.php`).
5. **Multisite.** The root file serves every site in the network. Write the Tutor copy only when every site with Tutor Pro has the add-on on. Otherwise skip, and note it in Hosting needs.
6. **Unwritable root.** If the root is not writable, do nothing. Show one line in Hosting needs with the manual step.
7. **Hosting needs.** When the add-on is on and the site has 0 published courses (`courses` post type), suggest turning it off: push notifications serve course students only.

Check before relying on it: does Apache/LiteSpeed serve the static file before WordPress's rewrite? The standard `!-f` condition should make it do so. The response should have no `x-litespeed-cache` and no PHP `x-powered-by`.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`: reference pattern for the existing Tutor fix and its settings text.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`: the two notes.
- `uninstall.php`
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: one line under Fixes for other plugins.

## Verification

title: Keep pages cached: limit concurrent fills per hosting account; main pages only where search engines are off
body:
## What happens

On one shared hosting account (CloudLinux + LiteSpeed, 6 cores) that runs 24 multisite networks with SEO Pro Stack, every fleet-wide plugin or theme release purges each network's page cache in turn. "Keep pages cached" then refills every network at the same time:

- Each network's main site, from the host's cron job every 5 minutes, opens pages one at a time for `CLI_BUDGET` (90 s); every page is a full uncached render in a web PHP worker (twice where a phone copy is kept).
- A full fill is up to `MAX` (1,000) pages per site plus translated copies: the last fills opened 1,000–5,624 pages per main site; at 21:47 UTC on 9 November 2026, 20 networks had 145–944 URLs queued (about 12,000 in total).
- A read-only process sample (30 × 2 s) counted running web PHP mostly on the networks purged last; `ps` showed 14 web workers at 35–60% CPU each, 20–95 s old.
- The host's support says the account-wide LiteSpeed denial seen that day (`403 Access to this resource on the server is denied!` / `.lsrecap` on every site of the account, including unrelated single sites) is CloudLinux/LiteSpeed CPU protection, triggered when the account repeatedly reaches its CPU limit; there is no allowlist.

`run()` stops a batch only when a page is refused (403/429/503), i.e. after the account is already over its limit. Nothing limits how many installs on one account fill at once, and sites hidden from search engines (staging/review copies) fill all 1,000 pages although no crawler or visitor needs the rest of the site.

## Proposed change

Files: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php` (`run()` ~L470, `CLI_BUDGET` L100), `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php` (`done()`, `GAP`), `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-pages.php` (`MAX` L54, `MAIN_MAX` L28).

1. **Account-wide fill slots.** Before a batch opens pages, take a non-blocking `flock()` on one of N slot files shared by every install running as the same system user (e.g. in `sys_get_temp_dir()`, named with the user id; under CageFS `/tmp` is per account). Default 2 slots, filter `seoprostack_keep_cached_slots`. With no free slot the batch opens nothing and is rescheduled after `GAP`, without counting as a stop. Release the slot at the end of the batch.
2. **Main pages only where search engines are off.** When `blog_public` is `0`, plan only the main pages (`MAIN_MAX`), not the rest of the site; filter `seoprostack_keep_cached_max` (default `MAX`, or `MAIN_MAX` on such sites) lets a site choose either way.
3. **Slow answers end the batch.** If a page takes longer than a threshold to build (e.g. 8 s, filterable), end the batch after it and wait `GAP`: a slow render is the earliest sign of a busy account, well before a refusal.

## Verification

- Two installs on one account, slots = 1: run `wp cron event run seoprostack_keep_pages_cached` on both at once after a purge; the second opens no pages and its next event is about `GAP` later.
- A site with `blog_public` 0: after Purge All, `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_queue` holds at most `MAIN_MAX` URLs; a public site still plans up to `MAX`.
- Plugin lint/PHPCS as for other releases; no change on single sites with search engines on and one install per account.

title: Keep pages cached: no could_not_set log line when a purge moves the batch during a cron run
body:
## What happens

Sites with **Keep pages cached** on log this line from WordPress's `wp-cron.php` when a cache purge lands during a cron run:

```
Cron unschedule event error for hook: seoprostack_keep_pages_cached, Error code: could_not_set, Error message: The cron event list could not be saved., Data: {"schedule":false,"args":[]}
```

Measured on our own Hostinger sites (LiteSpeed, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.191, WordPress 7.1.4), counting `could_not_set` lines for this hook in each site's `error_log`: 1 on 8 November, 67 in English on 9 November (plus the same line in Dutch and French, about 70 in all), across 20 sites, after Keep pages cached was turned on for a group of busy multisite networks whose builders purge the cache many times an hour. The other hooks' `could_not_set` lines fell away after #1232: `mwai_tasks_internal_run` had 167 unschedule lines on 5 November, 1 on 8 November and none on 9 November.

## Why (confirmed in code)

1. `wp-cron.php` reads the due events once, at its start.
2. A purge in another request calls `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Queue::fill_later()` → `save($queue, DELAY, true)`, which clears the due event and schedules it `DELAY` seconds later, so the fill runs after LiteSpeed applies the purge.
3. `wp-cron.php` then calls `wp_unschedule_event($timestamp, $hook, $args, true)` for the copy it read. `SEOProStack_Cron_List::write()` applies the removal to the stored list, which no longer has the event, so the merged list equals the stored one; the database update changes no rows, `update_option()` returns false, and core logs `could_not_set`.
4. `SEOProStack_Keep_Pages_Cached::run()` then sees the moved event (`SEOProStack_Cron_List::next_stored()`, #1362) and leaves it to run at its new time. **Nothing is lost**: the line is noise, but it is SEO Pro Stack's noise, it hides real errors, and the deploy check counts it.

The same happens whenever two requests remove the same event (two cron runners that read the same due event).

## Fix

In `includes/class-seoprostack-cron-list.php`, add a `pre_unschedule_event` filter (registered in `init()` beside `write()`): when the event (time, hook, hash of its arguments) is no longer in the list as stored now (`stored()`), it is already unscheduled, so return `true` and drop the option caches as `write()` does when another request already applied a change (#1270), so the rest of the request reads the stored list. When the stored list cannot be read, or still has the event, return the filter's value unchanged and let core remove it.

- Files: `includes/class-seoprostack-cron-list.php` (new filter method, `init()`), `changelog.txt` (Unreleased).
- Pattern: `SEOProStack_Cron_List::write()` and `next_stored()` in the same file.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- On the test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`): `wp eval` that schedules a single event in the past, reads the list (so the request has its copy), removes the event from the stored `cron` option with a direct database update, then calls `wp_unschedule_event($time, $hook, array(), true)`: before the fix it returns `WP_Error` `could_not_set`; after, `true`, and `wp cron event list` shows no copy of the event. Normal unscheduling (event still stored) still removes it.
- After deploy: no new `could_not_set` lines for `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached` in the sites' `error_log` over a day of purges.

title: Image loading: choose Kadence background copies by the pixels they paint, without the 10% margin
body:
## What

Image loading's four scripts that choose a copy of a Kadence Blocks background picture take the narrowest copy at least as wide as the device pixels it paints **× 1.1** ("10% to spare for fonts and late styles", GH#1221). The margin is not needed for sharpness and costs bytes on common screens: it pushes the choice up a size whenever the painted width is within 10% below a copy's width.

The most common case is PageSpeed's phone (412 px, DPR 1.75): a full-width picture paints 721 device pixels, and 721 × 1.1 = 793 is wider than WordPress's 768 copy (`medium_large`), so the 1024 copy is taken. Likewise a 768 px tablet at DPR 2 paints 1,536 and gets the next size up instead of the 1536 copy (the GH#1221 test noted "the full picture at 768 (1,536, within the 10%)"), and so do 1440 and 1920 px desktops at DPR 1.

Browsers choosing from `srcset` take the narrowest candidate at least as wide as the painted device pixels, with no margin. The scripts already swap in a larger copy when the box grows (ResizeObserver) or the pixel ratio changes (`matchMedia` resolution), so a box that grows after fonts load still gets enough pixels. Never less sharp: every file stays at least as wide as the pixels it paints.

## Evidence (10 November 2026, 1.3.192, production pages through a local proxy that removes only the `* 1.1`)

- Sharpness probe (Playwright, 5 screens: 412×823@1.75, 393×852@3, 768×1024@2, 1440×900@1, 1920×1080@1; 7 Kadence home pages): every background picture the scripts set was at least as wide as the device pixels it paints, with and without the margin. Without it, smaller files were chosen in 11 of 25 page-screen cases with a sized picture (for example phone 1536→1024, tablet full→1536, 1440 desktop full→1536 or 2048→1536, 1920 desktop full→2048); none larger. No second fetch of the same element.
- Local Lighthouse (mobile, simulated throttling), alternating runs:
  - Home page opening with a full-width Advanced Slider (400 px high): slide 1536 copy (80 KB AVIF) → 1024 copy (19 KB AVIF; 933 device pixels painted). LCP 4,012–4,686 ms (median 4,023) → 3,683–3,776 ms (median 3,710), score 75–85 → 84–87, 5 pairs.
  - Home page opening with a full-width row (16:9): 1024 copy (104 KB) → 768 copy (77 KB; 721 device pixels painted); images 360 → 291 KB; LCP 3,207–4,385 ms → 3,543–3,556 ms, 3 pairs.
  - Three other home pages whose pictures are not near a copy's width: same files, differences within runner noise.

## Files to change

- `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-hero.php` (`need()`, line ~236; docblock line ~12)
- `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-slider.php` (`need()`, line ~398; docblock line ~34)
- `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-rows.php` (`size()`, line ~471; docblock line ~35 and comment ~463)
- `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-early.php` (head script, line ~214; docblock line ~24). The head and the scripts after the block must use the same rule, or the head's copy is not taken and the picture is fetched twice.
- `README.md` (the four Image loading bullets that say "with 10% to spare"), `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`.
- Test site (or proxy) at the five screens above: every chosen file at least as wide as the painted device pixels; the head's copy is taken by the script after the block (fetched once); growing the box or the pixel ratio still swaps in a larger copy.
- After release and deploy: keyed PageSpeed mobile on the Kadence home pages.
